nominatim scribimus, quos videre potuerimus, aut ipsi discutimus. Venit ad festivitatem vir quidam ex Biturigo manibus debilis, cuius digiti in palma erant
defixi in tantum, ut putaretur vermibus scatere. Sed, celebrata solemnitate, directis ambarum manuum digitis, incolomitati donatus est; viditque eum omnis
populus sospitem redeuntem. Cui causa debilitatis ex hoc contigit, quod saepem segitis die dominico conponere voluisset.

### 46

**[046]** Mulier ex Pectavo terreturio, cuius brachium contractis nervis emarcuerat, ad sepulchrum beati viri veniens, in oratione vigiliisque pernoctans,
brachium sanum retulit; sed ilico a dominis in servitio mancipata, cadem incurrit. Revertitur igitur et sanatur. Tunc venientes domini eius et eam abducere
nitentes, accepto de rebus sancti pretio, quieverunt, et ita haec libertati donatur.

### 47

**[047]** Hisce diebus cum quidam pro dissolvendo debito, quod in necessitatibus suis contracxerat, interpellaretur, nec esset virtus atque facultas ad
reddendum quae mutuaverat, in carcere coartatur. Denique, cum videret creditor, quod ei nihil extorqueri possit, quia nihil habebat, nec esset qui ei manum
misericordiae porregeret, artius cum in vincula constringit, negatoque cibo potuque, dicebat: 'Ego te faciam ad omnium documentum fame tabescere, donec omnia
reddas'. Haec autem cum agerentur, sancti antistitis reliquiae, quae Sessionico in pago ferebantur, per plateam praeteribant. Auditasque vinctus psallentium
voces, oravit, ut eum virtus sancti antistitis visitaret; statimque dissolutis ligaminibus, nullo retcnente, basilicam sanctam ingreditur. Dehinc a devotis
redemptus, a nexu debiti absolutus est.

### 48

**[048]** Factum est autem in una festivitatum, ut mulier, quae perdito lumine in caecitate durabat, audita sancti viri miracula, alacri devotione basilicam
eius expeteret. Prostrata autem super aridam humum ante sepulchrum, mox ut orationem fudit lumen recipere meruit.

### 49

**[049]** In hac solemnitate advenit puerolus, oculorum obtutibus clausis, aurium aditibus oppilatis, oris officiis obstructis, manuum usibus perditis, pedum
gressibus condemnatis. Quid plura? Ita erat omnium membrorum usu praemortuus, ut solo spiritu palpitaret. Ut autem locum sanctum attigit, omni prorsus
debilitate submota, cum gratiarum actione sanus abscessit.

### 50

**[050]** Lupus Burdegalensis urbis presbiter quodam tempore graviter a quartano typo vexabatur, ita ut, accedente febre, neque cibum neque potum sumere possit.
Interea advenit festivitas sancti Martini antestitis. At ille, celebratas cum reliquo clero vigilias, mane praecedit omnes et ad basilicam sancti festinat. Dum
autem properat, obvium habuit Iudaeum; quo inquerente, quo pergeret, respondit: 'Typum quartanum incurri, et nunc ad basilicam sancti propero, ut me virtus eius
ab hac infirmitate discutiat'. Qui ait: 'Martinus enim nihil tibi proderit, quem terra obpremens terreum fecit; casso eius aedem expetis; nou enim poterit
mortuus viventibus tribuere medicinam'. At ille dispiciens verba serpentis antiqui, abiit quo coeperat, et prostratus coram sanctis pignoribus, orationem fudit,
repperitque ibi duas candelulas ex cera ac papiro formatas. Quibus adsumptis, ad domum exhibet, inluminatisque eis, favillam papiri cum aqua munda hausit, mox
sanitatem recepit. Iudaeus vero ab hac infirmitate correptus, per anni spatium ventilatus est; sed mens iniqua nec tormentis mutari potuit umquam.

### 51

**[051]** Chardegysilus vero Sanctonicae urbis civis cognomento Gyso, susceptis nobis ad domum suam, invitat ad oratorium, quod mater eius aedificatum beati
Martini reliquiis consecravit. Denique cum, expleta oratione, solliciti essemus, si ibidem virtus antistitis ostensa fuisset, respondit: 'Ante annum tertium
puerulus iste filius meus, quem coram cernitis, cum adhuc ad matris penderet papillam, incomode agere coepit ac per triginta dies aut eo amplius inter manus non
sine labore deportabatur, donec ita addictus est, ut nec mammellam valeret sugere nec alium cibum. Deficiente autem eo, iam die sexto, postquam gravius agere
coepit, deposuimus cum ante altare, flentes atque eius obitum praestolantes. Ego autem dolorem non ferens, discessi a domo, mandans mulieri, ut, cum obiret,
statim eum sepulturae locaret. Flente autem genetrice, iacuit infans usque ad vesperum. Cadente autem sole, elevat vocem suam, dicens: „Dulcissima soror, ubi
es?" Sic enim genetricem, ut blandicia infantum habet, vocitare solitus erat. At illa accurrit, dicens: „Adsum, fili dulcissime", susceptoque eum in ulnis,
moxque porrecta papilla, hausto lac, convaluit'.

### 52

**[052]** His diebus quando nobis haec relata sunt unus clericorum nostrorum ventris fluxum incurrit cum febre ac nimia defectione stomachi; et quae proiciebat
per inferiorem partem, para maxima cruor erat. Et ea causa eum magis afficerat, quia cibum quod accipiebat, invalescente nausia, statim reiciebat; sed protinus
ut de sepulchri pulvere bibit, omni infirmitate dempta, firmatus est.

### 53

**[053]** Sed nec hoc silendum putavi, quod saepius in morte praecipites, extenta pietatis dextera, sublevavit. Denique Genitoris civis nostri servus a iudice
pro furti scelere conprehensus, patibulo diiudicatar. Qui cum duceretur, nomen beati antistitis invocabat, dicens: 'Libera me, sancte confessor Martine, ab
inminente periculo'. Adpensus igitur ac solus relictus, commoto subito vento, audivit vocem dicentem: 'Liberemus eum'. Et ecce a quattuor partibus caeli
concussus stipis, qui hominem sustentabat, cum inmenso cespite in modum arboris eradicatae a terra divellitur, et sic homo morti deditus redivivus eregitur.
Alius quoque, qui multa fecerat scelera, et conpunctus a Deo, paenitentiam pro malis quae gesserat agebat, adprehensus sine causa, simili nece damnatur,
invocans semper beati confessoris auxilium. Qui cum adpensus fuisset, disruptis vinculis, inlaesus ad terram ruit. Sed mala mens hominum iterum adpendit, quem
Dens eripuit. Quod audiens abba monasterii a loco proximi, currit ad comitem, rogaturus pro eo, – erat enim exinde quasi tribus milibus –, obtentaque cum eo rei
huius vita, rediit vivumque repperit. Quo a suspendio deposito, adduxit ad monasterium profitentem atque dicentem, quia: 'Sensi virtutem sancti Martini, qui me
eripuit'.

### 54

**[054]** Erat enim homo infra terminum ipsius Turonicae urbis ex vico Montis Laudiacensis, et homo ille erat natura simplex, nexus vinculo coniugali. Cui cum
coniuge quiescente nocte media pavor exoritur; exterritus ac de lectulo exiliens, dum per hospitiolum suum vagatur trepidus, vocis perdidit famulatum. Nec
moratus, indicat nutu coniugi, ut eum ad sancti basilicam exhiberet. Qui adveniens, dum ante beatum sepulchrum per sex decubat assidue menses in oratione,
absoluta lingua, eloquium, sicut antea habuerat, recipere meruit virtute beati.

### 55

**[055]** Mulier Transligeritana die dominico cum operam exerceret, quam in die illo fieri patrum inhibebat auctoritas, manus eius contracta diriguit, digitique
in palmam difixi sunt. Quae dum doloribus cruciaretur, ad sanctam aedem confessoris accessit vovitque, ut, si ab hac sanaretur infirmitate, nullum opus deinceps
in hac dominicae resurrectionis ageret die, quod huic diei esset incongruum; statimque amotis digitis a palma, manu directa discessit.

### 56

**[056]** Magna est enim pietas confessoris, quae sic arguit insipientes, ut ponens vitium ante oculos reddat in posterum emendatos. Pro hac causa mulier alia
debilitatur. Nam cum die sabbati post solis occasum, quod adiacit resurrectionis dominicae nocti, panem forno locaret, brachium eius dolore quatitur.
Iniectumque alium et tertium panem, manus invita lignum quod tenebat coepit adstringere; intellegensque mulier divinae se virtutis [iudicio] condemnari,
velociter palam quam tenebat abiecit; nihilhominus non effugire potuit poenam. Nam ita manus eius cum gravi dolore contractae sunt, ut ungulae in ipsa
difigerentur palma. Ex hoc nullus medici se credens posse fomento sanari, beati basilicam expetivit, ibique fideliter orans, directis manibus sanata discessit,
vovitque, ut per singulos menses una ebdomada ad sanctum templum debeat deservire. Quod per unum annum eam observasse, manifestissime cognitum est. Post annum
vero, intermissa unius mensis ebdomada, non accessit ad basilicam sanctam. Sedenti vero in hospitiolo suo, oculus ei a dolore transfigitur. Illum quoque
conpremens et alius dolere coepit extemplo. In unius horae momento caeca ab oculis ambobus efficitur. Nec mora, confessa ad praesidia nota confugit; ibique
orationem suppliciter fundens ac paenitentiam pro neglegentia conpunctae agens, die octava, sanguine ab oculis profluente, inluminata est.

### 57

**[057]** Hominis cuiusdam oculi crassa caliginis nube contecti, quodam gluttino coniunctis palpebribus fuerant obserati, et quod super deerat viro, magnis
doloribus tenebatur. Quid plura? Festivitatem sancti cum reliquis devotus expetiit, adtente exorans, ut a virtute beati antistitis visitari mereretur in die
solemnitatis. Sed sacra solemnia praevenit potentia confessoris, ostendens se adesse populis, cum tenebras pepulit lumenque refudit. Igitur ante diem tertium
festivitatis hoc in atrio, quod absidam corporis ambit, orante, subito aperti sunt oculi eius, et aspiciens lucem videre meruit. Quod cum his qui aderant cum
gratiarum actione narraret, dictum est ei, ut silens potius orationem funderet, ut coeptam virtutem beatus antistis celerius adimpleret. Tunc prostratus terrae,
cum in lacrimis prorupisset, firmatis oculis, incolomis a solo surrexit.

### 58

**[058]** Post diem vero tertium huius solemnitatis erat quidam paralyticus hoc in loco exorans, cui debilitas hac de causa, ut ipse enarravit, evenerat. Dum
esset, inquit, puer parvulus et cum reliquis pecorum in campo custodiam gereret, super fontem quondam obdormivit; aliis quoque ad meridiem recedentibus, hic
solus remansit. Tandemque relictus a somno, dum consurgere nititur, doloribus coartatur. Mox membris omnibus contractis ac retortis extrorsum brachiis,
contractis in poplite nervis, calcaneis ad crura deductis, cum nulla esset virtus eundi, inmensae ab eo lacrimae cum magnis vocibus effluebant. Reversis autem
sociis ad visenda pecora, hic heiulans invenitur. Dehinc parentum ulnis ablatus, domui restituitur. Post dies vero paucos cum parumper a doloribus laxaretur,
mendicis quibusdam deputatus est, cum quibus per decim aut eo amplius annos regiones urbesque circumiens, ad hanc festivitatem adveniens, membris omnibus
solidatus est. Duo eadem die caeci inluminati; duo inergumini ad sepulchrum antistitis emundati sunt.

### 59

**[059]** Adolescens quidam ex nostris nocturnis febribus vexabatur in tantum, ut ab hora diei octava usque in crastinum secunda diei hora nullam aestuandi
quietem possit accipere. Erat enim ei et horribile omne cibum, nec quicquam unde confortaretur accipiebat. Dolor etiam saevus membra omnia quatiebat, sed et
pallor genas obsederat. Dumque sic inter manus ferreretur parentum ut aeger, aegre obtenere potui, ut ad sepulchrum beati antestitis deferretur. Tandem adlatus,
de sacrosancto tumuli pulvere deluto potui sumpsit; mox ab hac benedictione, fugato universo dolore, febris extincta est. Nec mora, secreta digestionum loca
puer expetit, deducitur in angulo ventris purgandi gratia. Verum ubi voluntatem alvi flatu inpellente profudit, statim duo vermes ab eo in modum serpentium
processerunt, qui ita moveri oculis hominum videbantur, ut vivere putarentur. His igitur ab eo digestis, ilico adplene sanatus, et cibum, ut solitus erat,
hausit et potum, ruborque genis, fugato pallore, redditur, membrisque omnibus solidatur.

### 60

**[060]** Oportunitatis causa nuper exteterat, ut ad visitandam genetricem meam in terretorium Cavellonensis urbis adirem. Sed metuens superventuras
infirmitates, de hoc pulvere, id est sepulchri beati antestitis, auferre et mecum deferre praesumpsi, scilicet ut, cum quempiam nostrorum morbus aliquis
invasisset, virtus sancti ope consuetudinaria subveniret. Igitur, ubi ad matrem accessi, protinus unum puerum febris cum disenteria arripuit, adterit et
consumit, ita ut, negato usu vescendi, de solis febribus aleretur. Die tertia cum haec audissem, delutum pulverem ad bibendum porrego moribundo, statimque
fugata febre, sedato dolore, convaluit. His diebus a Verano antitiste audivi, quod quodam tempore, dum typi quartani aestu uriretur, expetita beati Martini
basilica, quae in loco illo erat, celebrata vigilia, fuisse sanatum. Nos vero ex hoc itinere Arverno venientes, repperimus Avitum episcopum a tertiano typo ita
graviter concuti, ut, etiam ei aliquid cibi sumeret, statim reiceret; sed de hoc pignore potui sumptu, calcata febre, roboratus est. Duos ex pueris nostris
valitudinaria febris invaserat, omniumque membrorum iuncturas, ut ex hoc contagio plerumque adsolet, dolor saevus obsederat; sed ab hac benedictione potati,
sanati sunt. Ego ipse in hoc itinere, cum dolorem dentium graviter sentirem, et iam non solum ipsi dentes, sed omne caput venarum pulsibus ac dolorum spiculis
figeretur, ac timpora valide prosilirent, hoc praesidium expetii, sed mox, dolore depresso, convalui. O tyriacam inenarrabilem! O pigmentum ineffabile! O
antidothum laudabile! O purgatorium, ut ita dicam, caeleste! Quod medicorum vincit argutias, aromatum suavitates superat ungentorumque omnium robor
supercrescit; quod mundat ventrem ut agridium, pulmonem ut hisopum, ipsumque caput purgat ut pyretrum. Etiam non solum membra debilia solidat, sed, quod his
omnibus magis est, ipsas illas conscientiarum maculas abstergit ac levigat. Sufficiant ergo haec huic libello, quae indita sunt. Tamen, si adhuc miracula
cernere meremur, placet ea alteri libello inseri, ut ea quae ostenduntur non oculi, sed magis debeant populari. De cetera vero virtutem eius deposcimus, ut qui
talia praestat ex tumulo nos iam a peccatis Deo mortuos suscitare dignetur mortis istius de sepulchro, ut in illo resurrectionis carnis omni tempore nobis
obteneat indulgentiam, cum iile provehitur ad coronam. EXPLICIT LIBER III.

## LIBER IV

### PREFACE

**[000]** Saluberrimo nos hortatu propheta admonet, dicens: Honorandi sunt amici tui, Deus. Nihilhominus et in alio psalmo: Qui timentes Dominum magnificat,
beatitudine copulatur domus aeternae. Ergo perspicue patet intellectui humano, quod admoneantur quique non solum inmunes a crimine, verum etiam noxialis
criminis malo dediti, cultum reverentes reddere amicis Dei. Quae res non solum in praesenti saeculo tribuit beneficium, verum etiam praestat et refrigerium in
futuro. Nam cum saepe videamus virtutum insignia prodere de tumulis beatorum, non inmerito commovemur debitam eis honoris reverentiam inpendere, a quibus non
desistimus infirmitatum remedia flagitare. Quorum precibus et ipsam peccaminum remissionem non dubitamus adipisci et non modo hanc mereri, verum ab infernalibus
suppliciis eorum interventu salvari. Confidimus enim, quod, sicut hic morborum genera resecant, illic saevas tormentorum poenas avertant, et, sicut hic mitigant
febres corporeas, illinc restingant aeternas, et, quomodo hic luridae leprae ulcera sordentia mundant, illic delictorum maculas mederi suo interventu obteneant,
ac, sicut hic mortuorum cadavera ad vitam resuscitant, illic peccato sepultos, ex Acharonticis stagnis manu iniecta erutos, vitae aeternae restituant. Quocirca,
dum unusquisque laetificatur in gaudio proprio sub patrono, tunc inpensius honorem reddit debitum, cum se senserit ab infirmitate qua detenebatur eius virtute
mundatum; sicut nunc de beato ac toto orbi peculiare patrono Martino antistite et nos et innumeri populi sunt experti; et utinam ignavia mentis nostrae
permitteret eum sic venerari, ut decet amicum Dei, qui, tantis in nos morborum obpressis generibus, plerumque restituit sanitati!

### 1

**[001]** Nuperrimo autem tempore ventris dolorem incurri. Et licet non usquequaque dabat solutionem, tamen doloris malum in illis interaneorum flexuosis
recessibus vagabatur. Adhibui, fateor, saepius balneas atque res calidas super ipsas alvi torturas ligari faciebam, sed nihil mederi poterat infirmitati. Sexta
etenim dies inluxerat, quod magis ac magis dolor invalescebat, cum mihi venit in memoria, ante paucos annos, sicut in libro secundo huius operis contenetur
scriptum, me ab hoc dolore sancti virtute fuisse sanatum. Accessi temerarius ad locum sepulchri, proiectusque solo, orationem fudi atque, secretius a
pendentibus velis unum sub vestimento iniectum, crucis ab hoc signaculum in alvo depinxi; protinus dolore sedato, sanus abscessi.

### 2

**[002]** Quodam vero tempore lingua mihi graviter inriguerat, ita ut plerumque, dum loqui velim, balbutire me faceret, quod non mihi sine inproperio erat.
Accessi autem ad tumulum sancti ac per lignum cancelli linguam impeditam traxi; protinus tumore conpresso, convalui. Intumuerat enim valide et totum palati
repleverat antrum. Deinde post die tertio labium mihi exilire graviter coepit. Accessi iterum quaerere sospitatem ad tumulum; tactamque a dependentibus velis,
protinus stetit venae pulsus. Et credo, mihi haec ex abundantia sanguinis evenisse; non tamen sanguinem minuere studui propter sancti virtutem. Nullam tamen
mihi ultra molestiam fecit haec causa.

### 3

**[003]** Denique puerulus parvulus gravabatur a febre et, exaesis membris, cum nullum acciperet cibum, in hoc erat, ut spiritum exalaret. Concurrit ad me pater
cum lacrimis; cui ego indicavi, ut, delatum ad basilicam, nocte tota vigilaret Quod cum fecisset, statim puerum sanum per virtutem antestitis sancti recepit.

### 4

**[004]** Ad festivitatem vero, quae mense quinto celebratur, adveniens quidam, cuius digiti in palma contraxerant; oratione facta, digitis directis, abscessit.
Mulier vero caeca post octo annos, prostrata solo coram sancti sepulchro, inluminatis oculis, repedavit in locum suum. Tres tunc inergumini sancti virtute
mundati sunt.

### 5

**[005]** Eo anno, id est Childeberthi regis tertio decimo, ad festivitatem, quae de beato eius transitu celebratur, servus Theudulfi civis Turonici custus
suillac, dum nocte circa gregem creditum excubaret, ne quiddam ex co aut bestia raperet, aut fraus furis auferret, oculis subita caligine interfusis, lumen
amisit. Qui per sex annos in caecitate durans, ad hanc festivitatem advenit; post tertium vero diem sancti virtute inluminatus, a domino est dimissus ingenuus.

### 6

**[006]** Anno quoque quarto decimo regis supradicti, adveniente solemnitate sancti, duodecim paralytici directi, tres caeci inluminati, quinque inergumini
emundati sunt. Adfuit huic festivitati et Aridius Lemovicinae urbis abba, cui in superioribus libellis meminimus, per quem Dominus paralyticam unam, quae per
octo annos carrucae superposita in atrio beati confessoris decubuerat, directis vestigiis, restauravit. Nam adserebat ipse vir Dei, sensisse se quasi beati
Martini manum, cum infirmae membra, inposito signo crucis, tactu salutari palparet. Advenerat etiam in hac festivitate et Florentianus maior cum Romulfo palatii
comite. Quibus non parva admiratio fuit de gloria confessoris, per quem Dominus talia tunc miracula dignatus est operare.

### 7

**[007]** Et quia Florentiani maioris memoriam fecimus, quid ab eo didicerim, nefas puto taceri. Tempore quodam causa legationis Galliciam adiit, atque ad
Mironis regis praesentiam accedens, negotia patefecit iniuncta. Erat enim co tempore Miro rex in civitate illa, qua decessor eius basilicam sancti Martini
aedificaverat, sicut in libro primo huius operis exposuimus. Ante huius aedis porticum vitium camera extensa per traduces dependentibus uvis quasi picta
vernabat. Sub hac enim erat semita, quae ad sacrae aedes valvas peditem deducebat. Cumque rex sub hac praeteriens orationis gratia hoc templum adiret, dixit
suis: 'Cavete, ne contingatis unum ex his botrionibus, ne forte offensam sancti antistitis incurratis. Omnia enim quae in hoc habentur atrio ipsi sacrata sunt'.
Haec audiens unus puerorum, ait infra se: 'Utrum sint haec huic sancto sacrata an non, ignoro. Unum scio, quia diliberatio animi est ab his vesci'. Et statim
iniecta manu caudam botrionis coepit incidere, protinusque dextera adhaerens camerae, arente lacerto, diriguit. Erat enim mimus regis, qui ei per verba
iocularia laetitiam erat solitus excitare. Sed non ei adiuvit cacinnus aliquis neque praestigium artis suae, sed, cogente dolore, voces dare coepit ac dicere:
'Succurrite, viri, misero, subvenite obpresso, relevamini adpenso et sancti antistitis Martini virtutem pro me deprecamini, qui tali exitu crucior, tali plaga
adfligor, tali incisione disiungor'. Egressus quoque rex, cum rem quae acta fuerat didicisset, tanto furore contra puerum est accensus, ut ei manus velit
abscidere, si a suis prohibitus non fuisset. Dicentibus tum praeterea famulis: 'Noli, o rex, iudicio Dei tuam adiungere ultionem, ne forte iniuriam, quam
minaris puero, in te retorqueas'. Tunc ille conpunctus corde, ingressus basilicam, prostratus coram altare sancto, cum lacrimis precem fudit ad Dominum, nec
ante a pavimento surrexit, quam flumen oculorum huius paginam delecti deleret. Quo a vinculo quo nexus fuerat absolute et in basilicam ingresso, rex elevatur a
solo, et sic recipiens incolomem famulum, palatium repetivit. Testabatur autem maior praefatus, haec se ab ipsius regis relatione·, sicut actum narravimus,
cognovisse. Sic enim gloriosus pontifex suam inlustrat urbem miraculis, ut deesse non sentiatur alienis.

### 8

**[008]** Praesenti vero anno Palladius Sanctonicae urbis episcopus sancti huius confessoris reliquias petiit. Construxerat enim in eius honore basilicam, quam
his pignoribus consecravit, meruitque ibi suscipere miracula, qua saepius urbs propria habet experta. Nam post duum aut trium mensuum curricula litteras eius
accepi, in quibus indicavit, tres paralyticos contractis pedibus advenisse, qui statim ut in basilicam ingressi orationem fuderunt, directis vestigiis, sanitati
sunt redditi. Duo caeci in eo loco lumen recipere, facta oratione, meruerunt, et amplius quam duodecim a febre frigoritica, depulso tremore, convaluerunt.

### 9

**[009]** Duo de pueris nostris, clericus scilicet Dagobaldus et laicus Theodorus, disenteriam cum febre patiebantur; in tantum lassati morbo erant, ut non
aliter nisi manibus aliorum, cum digestionis necessitas advenisset, ab stratu sublevarentur. Sed de sepulchri pulvere hausto, statim convaluerunt.

### 10

**[010]** Est apud nos patena colore sapphirino, quam dicitur sanctus de Maximi imperatoris thesauro detulisse, de qua super frigoriticos virtus saepe procedit.
Nam in accentu febrium quis positus, qui cum tremore fieri solet, advenerit, de ea aqua hauserit, mox sanatur. Est et apud Condatensim vicum alia aeque patena a
sancto exhibita metallocristallina, similem infirmis beneficium praebens, si fideliter expetatur. Bodilo unus de notariis nostris cum stomachi lassitudine animo
turbatus erat, ita ut nec scribere iuxta consuetudinem nec excipere, et quae ei dictabantur vix poterat recensere. Tunc cum saepius verbis increparetur, super
hanc beati viri patenam, quam nobiscum esse diximus, aquam fudit, ipsamque ore transponit. Mox sensui suo redditus, opus officii sagatius, quam consueverat,
expedibat.

### 11

**[011]** Sed quid mirum, si sensa adversitate turbata reddat hominibus, qui saepius sterilitatem in fecunditate convertit? Blidericus quidam Carnoteni
terretorii civis, accepta uxore, ut dono Dei procreationis suae prole ditaretur, orabat; sed nihil ex ea germinis merebatur accipere. Tricisimus etenim annus
curriculum expedierat, uxore sterili permanente, cum vir, saluberrime pro animae commodum tractans, ait uxori: 'Ecce saeculum, quod utimur, praeteriens est, et
nulla inter nos subolis gignitur, qui, nobis deficientibus, congestum laboris nostri debeat possedere. Accedam', inquit, 'ad basilicam sancti Martini et eam
faciam heredem mihi, ut, liberis abnegatis, vel cum eadem quae habere potero possedeam in futuro'. Consensit mulier sapiens viri prudentis consilio. Nec mora,
proceditur ad basilicam sancti, fusaquc oratione, invitat abbatem secum domi accedere. Quo accedente, tradidit ei omnem possessionem suam, dicens: 'Sint haec
omnia penes sancti Martini ditione quae habere videor, et hoc tantum exinde utar, ut de his, dum vixero, alar'. Consignatisque rebus, coegit abbatem manere ibi.
Mirum dictu! Post 30, ut diximus, annorum curricula, in ipsa qua res suas basilicae tradidit nocte cognovit uxorem suam, quae concipiens peperit filium. Sed et
deinceps alios habuit, quod non ambigitur, haec virtute sancti praestitum huic viro fuisse. Verumtamen non refragavit, acceptis filiis, promissionem homo ille,
sed eis alia loca tribuens, quae primum sancto largitus fuerat confirmavit.

### 12

**[012]** Apud Turnacensim vero Cenomanici terreturii villam, quae nunc in ipsius sanctae basilicae ditionibus retenetur, mulier quaedam diuturna caecitate
detenta et senio praegravata, ad oratorium villae ipsius resedens, dum stipem quaereret ac assidue sancti Martini nomen invocaret, quadam nocte dominica
coeperunt oculi eius a dolore conpungi. Tunc illa prostrata coram sancto altare, erumpente sanguine, lumen recepit. Verumtamen reliquiac in ipso loco
beatissimorum apostolorum, id est Petri et Pauli, habentur; sed haec asserebat virtute sancti antistitis fuisse sanatam. Verumtamen fides nostra retenet, in
multorum sanctorum virtutibus unum Dominum operari, et nec illos disiunctos virtutibus, quos caelo pares, miraculis Dominus aequales reddit in terris.

### 13

**[013]** Ad festivitatem vero illam, cui Aunacharius Autisioderensis urbis pontifex adfuit, quidam manum aridam contractamque detulit, sed post diem tertiam
festivitatis redintegratam domum reportavit.

### 14

**[014]** Baudegisilus quidam ex Andecavensis urbis terreturio, Baudulfi filius, vici Geinensis incola, dum humoris saevi iaculo sauciatur, debilitatus
occubuit. Isque cum a patre paupere sine operis beneficio pasceretur, ut basilicae sancti Martini limina oscularet, patrem lacrimis obortis efflagitat. Qui nec
mora in navi positum, quia vehi altera evectione non poterat, ante pedes sancti, id est foris sepulchrum, filium devotus exposuit. Qui per dies aliquos orationi
vacans et sancti auxilium poscens, amota debilitate, sanitati restituitur; sicque cum genitore domi incolomis restitutus est.

### 15

**[015]** In Ausciensi quoque terreturio erat homo Caelestis nomine, cui multa erant apium alvearia. Ex quibus cum examen egressum alta conscendens longa
conpeteret, et ille sequens nullum prorsus capiendi obteneret effectum, prostratus solo, sancti Martini invocat nomen, dicens: 'Si virtus tua, beatissime
confessor, hoc examen. retenere voluerit eumque ditioni meae reddiderit, quae in posterum ex eo procreata fuerint, mel usibus meis sumam, ceram vero ad
luminaria basilicae tuae cum omni soliditate diregam'. Haec effatus, cum adhuc terrae decumberet, statim examen apium super unam arbusculam, quae viro erat
proxima, decidit et insedit, collectumque et in alveare reconditum domi detulit. De quo infra duos aut tres annos multa congregavit Ex quibus cum iam amplius
quam ducentas cerae libras adgregatas haberet, rumor hostilitatis obortus est. At ille, ne votum suum perire cerneret, ceram fossa humo operuit. Pace quoque
reddita, diaconum nostrum, ut eam peteret, arcessivit. Erat tunc cum eo puer, qui renum gravissimum perferebat dolorem. Qui accedens ad virum et cognoscens ab
ore eius quae gesta fuerant, cera quae terra latebat detegi iubet. Puer vero, qui dolorem, quem diximus, patiebatur, accepto sarculo ut terram foderet, ait: 'Si
tu propitius es, sancte Martine, ad hoc munus hominis huius aspiciendum, contingat virtus tua renes meos, et sis mihi salus, cum hanc detexero ceram'. Et
percutiens sarculo terram, sonuit ossiculum renum eius, et statim omnis dolor ablatus est; et sic incolomis cum hac cera beatae basilicae praesentatus est.

### 16

**[016]** Homo quidam urbis Turonicae iudici culpabilis extetit, quem in vincula conpactum custodire praccepit. Advenientibus autem diebus sanctis dominicae
resurrectionis, iussit eum iudex ipse in ulteriorem Ligeris fluvii litus in alia retrudi custodia. Ducebatur igitur non solum catenis colla revinctus, verum
etiam post tergum manibus conligatis; cumque ad ripam nominati amnis advenissent et navigium, quo transire deberent, praestolarentur, atque ille sancti Martini
auxilium incessabiliter flagitaret, visum est repente custodibus, quasi ab aliquo capite verberati fuissent. Protinusque in terram ruunt, ac catenae, quae
vinctum tenebant hominem, confractae sunt, laxatae vero corrigiae de manu solvuntur. Ipse autem liberum se sentiens, decumbentibus adhuc solo hominibus,
secessit ab eis et sanctae cclesiae limen ingressus est, sicque a iudice relaxatur. Ferebant enim nonnulli, his diebus et apud Pectavensim urbem vinctos ab
ergastulo carcerali fuisse resolutos. Quod ambigeri non potest, quia utriusque confessoris virtus utramque urbem sacris potuit inlustrare miraculis.

### 17

**[017]** Puerolus parvulus nomine Leodoaldus·, servus cuiusdam Baudeleifi de vico Andecavensi, cui Crovio antiquitas nomen indidit, postquam renatus ex aqua et
Spiritu sancto cum reliquis infantibus ludum in platea exercens, ut aetas illa patitur, huc illucque discurreret, subito commotus cum impetu ventus et pulverem
elevans, oculos infantis implevit. Qui cum caecitate percussus doloribus cruciaretur, apparuit aviae eius vir quidam per somnium: 'Vade', inquit, 'ad basilicam
sancti Martini, et recipiet visum puer iste!' Nec morata mulier, fide plena venit ad festivitatem, recepitque inluminatum virtute pontificis nepotem suum.

### 18

**[018]** Huius etenim urbis terreturii puella Viliogundis vocabulo simili conditione caecatur. Dum enim cum reliquis puellulis per stratas villae ludum
exercendo discurreret, venti· violentia pulvere elevato, opplevit oculos eius. Quae statim doloribus vexata petiit parentes suos, ut eam ad basilicam sancti
Martini deducerent. Quo facto, protinus ut orationem pro ea fuderunt, inluminata est. Nobis quoque egredientibus de sanctis missarum solemnibus occurrerunt
simul praefatus puer atque puella, dicentes, se hora ipsa lumen virtute beati antistitis recepisse. Quod nobis magnum praestetit gaudium credentibus, quod nos
virtus beati confessoris sit visitare dignata.

### 19

**[019]** Litoveus autem quidam ex infantia sua membris debilis, accedente febre, caecatus est; sed ad superiorem festivitatem veniens, directis membris, lumen
tamen adhuc dempto, discessit. Sed cum ad hanc iterum regressus fuisset solemnitatem, exemptis tenebris, lumini datus exoritur.

### 20

**[020]** In hac etiam festivitate et Leudardus, servus Eumerii Namnetici urbis diaconi, cum per sex annos caecitatis fuisset catena constrictus, ad basilicam
accedens, virtute beati confessoris inluminatus est. Per visionem enim somnii admonitus fuerat, ut huius sancti auxilia flagitaret antistitis.

### 21

**[021]** Quidam de civibus Turonicis, dum ad regis occursum properaret, vas cum vino unumque panem ad sepulchrum una mansurum nocte deposuit, ut scilicet in
itinere positus hoc haberet salutis praesidium. Quae exinde adsumpta, iter carpere coepit. Factum est autem, ut metatum requirens, hominis cuiusdam ingrederetur
hospitium, depositisque sarcinis, mulier, quae habebat spiritum inmundum, beati Martini adventum vocibus inmensis adnuntiare coepit ac dicere: 'Quid nos
persequeris, sanctae? Quid nos crucias, serve Dei?' Tunc hospes ille qui venerat, accepto calice, paululum vini de vase illo auferens, frustram benedicti panis
effractam posuit in eo. Quod ubi mulier illa quae debacchabat accepit, mox cum sanguine eiecto daemonio salvata est. Alia in eo loco mulier, quae diu a frigoris
aegrotabat, accepto ab hac benedictione modico, ut sumpsit, sanata est.

### 22

**[022]** Silluvius incola Baiocassinus, cum in rure positus quiddam operaret, commoto vento, pavore perculsus, tremere coepit ac membris omnibus distitui,
vociferare etiam et sibi mortem inminere testabatur. Interea concurrentibus vicinis ad spectaculum tale, ipse inter voces et ululatus, contractis nervis,
debilitatur ad integre; et non solum ei usus aurium denegatur, verum etiam et ipsum lumen caruit oculorum. Post quindecim vero annos, dum in hac infelicitate
degeret, ad festivitatem sancti Martini veniens, solidatis membris oculisque receptis, abscessit.

### 23

**[023]** Nec dissimili virtute mulier Ermegundis Audecavensis civis, vici incola Croviensis, contracta ac caeca, in hac festivitate directa inluminataque
discessit. Sed et Charimundus ex Bricilonno debilis veniens, virtute beati antestitis redintegratus est.

### 24

**[024]** In huius etiam solemnitatis virtute nonnulli, cooperante Christi gratia, persenserunt. Nam Leodomundus caecus post septem annis, Domnitta post tres et
tres insuper alii caeci in hac festivitate visum per opem beati antistitis receperunt; inergumini plerique mundati sunt.

### 25

**[025]** Leonis presbiteri nostri vernacula, cum ad villulam urbi proximam parentibus· ulnis deportata secessisset, vi febris obpremitur et die ac nocte valde
in mortis discrimine cernitur. Quam videns presbiter exanimari violentia morbi, nocte ascenso equite, ad basilicam sancti confessoris accessit, pulsansque
ostium cellulae, in qua aedituus quiescebat, virum suscitare nequivit. Cumque basilicam sanctam ingredi non valeret, coram absida sepulchri fudit orationem,
collegitque parumper de pulvere terreno, quod secum fide plenus evexit, eumque dilutum, ut puellulae ad bibendum protulit, protinus febris abscessit.

### 26

**[026]** Fuerat nobis causa quaedam Childeberthi· regis adire praesentiam. Pergentibus quoque nobis, iter per pagum Remensem adgressi sumus, repperimusque
hominem quendam, qui nobis relatu suo, patefactum carcerem huius orbis, in quo inter reliquos vinctos huius famulus tenebatur, Martini virtute fuisse,
vinctosque ab ergastulo absolutes liberos abscessisse. Erat enim huiusmodi carcer, ut super struem tignorum axes validi superpositi pulpitarentur, ac desuper,
qui eosdem obpremerent, insignes fuerant lapides collocati. Nihil minus et ostium carceris, sera ferro munita, obducto clave pessulo obserabatur; sed virtus
antistitis, ut ipse relator asseruit, lapides dimovet, disicit pulpita, catenas confregit et trabem, quae vinctorum coartabat pedes, aperuit ac, nec reserato
ostio, homines per aera sublevatos foris tecto patente produxit, dicens: 'Ego sum Martinus, miles Christi, absolutor vester. Abscedite cum pace et abite
securi!' Sed cum nos ad regem accedentes huius virtutis diffamaremus miraculum, adfirmavit rex, quosdam ex his qui absoluti fuerant ad se venisse, atque
conpositionem fisco debitam, quam illi fretum vocant, a se fuisse reis indultam. Hoc autem factum est ante quattuor festivitatis dies in anno memorati regis
sexto et decimo.

### 27

**[027]** Adveniente autem festa beati, Nonnichius Namneticorum pontifex ad basilicam sancti advenit, exhibens secum puerum membris debilem nomine
Baudegisillum. Celebrata igitur solemnia sancti, hunc, artubus restitutis, secum reduxit incolomem.

### 28

**[028]** Nobis quoque cum rege morantibus, Claudius quidam ex cancellariis regalibus a febre corripitur. Cumque cibum potumque nimia oppressus febre
exhorruisset, nobis quae patiebatur quaestus est, delutumque pulverem, quod de sancto beati sepulchro pro salvatione levavimus, ut hausit, mox conpressa febre,
sanatus est.

### 29

**[029]** Venerabilis vero Agnes Pectavarum sanctimonialium abbatissa relatum sibi ab ipso cut contigit Treverico negotiatore, rem miraculi provenisse, sic
retulit: 'Dum', inquit, 'Mettis accessissem, appellat me negotiator, unde essem. Dixi: „De Pictavis". Dicit mihi, si aliquando ad basilicam beati Martini
Turonus occurrissem. Dixi, quod, quomodo in Austria ambularem, sic ibi me praesentassem. Dicit mihi, quale beneficium domni Martini senserat. Dum Mettis salem
negotiasset et ad pontem Mettis adplicuisset, dicit: „Domne Martine, me et puricellos quos haben et navicellam meam tibi conmendo". Inter hoc recubantes in
nave, omnes condormivimus. Mane excitans me cum puricellis quos mecum habebam, invenimus nos ante portam Trevericam, nescientes, quomodo venissemus, qui nos
adhuc Mettis credebamus consistere; qua ratione aut navigatum est aut volatum; sola conmendatione beati Martini nec fluvium sensimus et Mosellae tumescentes
undas naufragas evitamus, et, quod satis est, inter saxa nocturno tempore praeterimus incolomes, non nauta vigile, non vento flante, non remo ducente'.

### 30

**[030]** Tempore post habito, cum usque Pectavam accessissemus urbem, libuit gratia tantum orationis monasterium Locotigiacensim adire, quo congregata
monachorum caterva locaverat vir beatus. Ibi enim mortuum primum suscitasse legitur, et ex illo ad episcopatum ductus scribitur. Ergo desideratum ego expetens
locum, prosternor ad cancellos anguli, in quo dicitur defuncti spiritum reduxisse. Post effusis vero cum oratione lacrimis ac celebratas solemniter missas,
percunctor abbatem, si aliquod ibi Dominus miraculum ostendisset. Asseruitque ille coram qui aderant fratribus, plerumque ibi inluminare caecos ac debiles
integrari. 'Quid tamen nuper sit gestum, inquio, tibi, domne, quia sollicite inquiris, evolvam. Mulier quaedam vicina loci huius, paralysi humore perculsa,
officio membrorum omnium usquequaque perdiderat. Quae carrucae inposita, bubus trahentibus, ferebatur, circumiens domos divitum, ut inopiae suae expleret
necessitatem. Ergo dum delata ad hunc locum pavimento prosternitur, lento conamine accedens, velum quod sanctum tegebat cancellum devote osculatur, dicens: „Hic
te, beate confessor, adesse credo, hic te mortuum suscitasse testificor. Confido enim, quod, si volueris, poteris me salvare ac sanitati restituere, sicut
quondam, disruptis inferni faucibus, defuncti animam reduxisti". Haec effata, genas lacrimis rigabat ubertim, ac statim impleta oratione, quicquid aridum,
quicquid contractum, quicquid dissolutum fuit, redintegratum est mulieris in corpore a beati antistitis virtute'. Simili sorte et alius paralyticus ad hoc
accedens monasterium, ut velum ipsius cancelli attigit, amota omni debilitate, sanus abscessit. Distat autem ab urbe Pectava quasi stadia quadraginta.

### 31

**[031]** Exinde egressi, Sanctonicum terreturium ingressi sumus. Cumque in quodam convivio de beati Martini virtutibus fabularemur, haec mihi unus e civibus,
adfirmantibus aliis vera esse, fideliter retulit. Naiogialo villa est in hoc terreturio sita, ad quam cum sanctus Martinus adhuc superstes in corpore adiret,
obvium habuit virum exhibentem aquam cum vasculo. Erat enim puteus ille, de quo haec exhibebat, situs in valle quasi mille passus a villa, ex eo incolae haustam
deferebant aquam. Tunc ait vir Dei homini aquam ferenti: 'Quaeso, dilectissime, contene manum tuam et huic asello, quem sedeo, paululum aquae ad bibendum
indulge'. Qui ait: 'Si necessarium ducis animal tuum adaquare, accede ad puteum et hauriens dabis ei. Nam ego quod cum labore detuli non praebebo'. Et haec
dicens, praeteriit. Quo discedente, veniens mulier et ipsa deferens aquam in ulnam; dixit ei similiter vir Dei. Quae acsi Rebecca condam audiens nuntium Dei:
'Et tibi praebeo', ait, 'et asino tuo potum, nec mihi labor est, ut iterum hauriam. Tantum voluntas tua fiat, qui iter pergens necessitatem pateris'. Et posito
vasculo, dedit asino illi bibere. Quae, iterum haustam aquam, impleto vasculo, revertebatur ad villam. Quam prosequens sanctus, ait: 'Reddam tibi pro mercede
beneficium, quia adaquasti asinum meum'. Et, positis genibus in terra, oravit ad Dominum, ut loco illi fontis ostenderet venam. Ac statim consummata oratione,
disrupta terra, fontem inmensum populis admirantibus patefecit. Qui usque hodie beneficium praebet hominibus conmanentibus in agro illo. In huius enim fontis
ore est lapis in testimonium, qui vestigium retenet aselli illius, super quem sanctus sedit antistis.

### 32

**[032]** Nec illud silere puto, quod hoc tempore, cum Plato episcopatum Pectavae urbis adeptus est, virtus sancti fuit ostensa. Domus adiuncta eclesiasticae
domui incendio maximo cremabatur, ac scintillae cum carbonibus super domus eclesiae, vento inpellente, cadebant. Sed ille de pulvere beati sepulchri secum
habens, elevatum chrysmarium contra ignem, exortus subito veritus vento illi contrarius, flammas tecto eclesiastico defendens, alia pepulit in parte, et sic
domus eclesiae liberata est.

### 33

**[033]** Cum autem puer eius in valitudine acerbissima febre exustus iaceret in lectulo et iam quasi exanimis haberetur, ut de hoc pulvere· deluto porrexit
infirmo, protinus fugata febre, puer convaluit de labore. Sed ad basilicam sancti redeamus.

### 34

**[034]** Cum autem ante hos annos terrae motus magnus terram concuteret, cunctaque valde moverentur quasi in uno momento casura, Leodulfus quidam vehementer ab
eo excussus, non solum sensu multatur, sed etiam omnibus membris debilis est effectus. Qui Veniens ad basilicam sancti Turonus et orationi paucos dies
incumbens, et νοci redditur et sensu et membris omnibus quasi redivivus sospes est redditus.

### 35

**[035]** Nec illuc praetermittendum puto, quod innocenter homo accusatus per calumnias malorum adducebatur ad urbem vinctus loro, ut truderetur ergastulo.
Cumque ante basilicam sancti Petri apostoli in publicum adductus agerem devenisset, dissolutae sunt manus eius, dixitque custodibus: 'In hoc apparet me a culpa
quam dicitis esse inmunem, cum meae manus divinitus sunt solutae'. Tunc illi indignantes artius cum revinxerunt, et insuper adhuc alio loro ligamini adiecto, ut
ita dicam, vincula ipsa vinxerunt. Contigit autem eo tempore, ut nos de basilica sancti Martini per plateam veniremus. Hii autem cum nobis in obviam venientes
adpropinquarent, ut primum sancti basilicam homo vinctus aspexit, statim solutae sunt manus eius, exiliensque de caballo in quo sedebat, pedes nostros arripuit,
exponens, se iniuste damnari. Sicque, nobis cum iudice conloquentibus, absque fatigatione discessit.

### 36

**[036]** Coniux Serenati hominis nostri, cum de cultura, viro praemisso, rediret, subito inter manus dilapsa comitantium terrae corruit, ligataque lingua,
nullum verbum ex ore potens proferre, obmutuit Interea accedentibus hariolis ac dicentibus, eam meridiani daemonii incursum pati, ligamina herbarum atque
incantationum verba proferebant; sed nihil medicaminis iuxta morem conferre poterant periturae. Cumque familia mixto ululatu perstreperet, filius eius ad neptam
nostram Eusteniam anhelus occurrit, nuntians, matrem suam extremae vitae terminum attigisse. Quae adveniens ad aegrotam camque visitans, amotis ligaminibus quae
stulti indiderant, oleum beati sepulchri ori eius infudit ceraque sofivit. Mox sermone reddito, nequitiae dolo dirempto, aegra convaluit.

### 37

**[037]** Tempore autem, quo post obitum gloriosissimi regis Gunthramni Childebertus rex Aurilianensim urbem adivit, puerorum unus aulicorum graviter a typo
tertiano, accedentibus discedentibusque febrebus, tremore superveniente, quatiebatur. Id cum nobis fuisset quaestus, de pulvere sancti sepulchri porreximus;
quod hauriens, conpresso tremore, convaluit. In sequenti vero nocte, cum dies ille, quo frangi consueverat, advenisset, vidit per visum advenientem personam
teterrimam dicentemque sibi: 'Ecce iam tempus tui tremoris advenit, quid dissimulas? Age quod consuevisti!' Haec eo dicente, advenit vir quidam vultu
splendidus, caesariae niveus, vultu decorus, dicens ei: 'Ne tremueris, sed facito super frontem tuam signum venerandae crucis, statimque sanaberis'. In hac
visione expergefactus, munitus hoc signaculo, quo fuerat iussus, numquam ulterius quae pertulerat passus est. Ab hoc tipo reginae puella fatigata, potu huius
sancti medicaminis sumptum, sanata est.

### 38

**[038]** Non post multos dies, cum solemnitas sancti dies annuus retulisset, nos a rege regressi, festivitati adfuimus, in qua quattuor caeci, lumine recepto,
regressi sunt, duo inergumini mundati, duo paralytici contracti, restitutis gressibus, incolomes redierunt.

### 39

**[039]** Post paucos vero dies cum culpabiles quosdam urbis Turonicae iudicis sententia carcerali ergastulo conclusisset, lamentantibus vinctis, virtus beati
confessoris apparuit, quae, disruptis vinculis compeditorum, liberos in basilicam abire permisit. Sicque et hii a iudice relaxati, ad propria abscesserunt.

### 40

**[040]** Quidam in regione Cantabriae Mauranus nomino manc a lectulo consurgens, dum de domo egreditur, visum est ei quasi ab aliquo percussus fuerit in
cervicem. Qui protinus ruens in terram, factus est tamquam mortuus, ac per triduum solo spiritu vivens, tamquam mortuus putabatur. Quarta autem die apertis
oculis, nihil poterat loqui. Ablata enim ei fuerat fandi facultas. Auditis enim beati Martini miraculis, unum triantem nautis porregit, innuens cum
supplicatione, ut eum ad beati antistitis templum deferrent. Quibus abeuntibus, ille ad domum suam reversus, vidit ante pedes suos aureum in similitudine
triantis. Quo adsumpto pensatoque, unius solidi appensus est pondere. Quod ille cernens, dixit intra se: 'Reddidit mihi virtus beati Martini meritum pro fenore,
quod eius templo direxi'. Et accensus desiderio, voluit in unam atque aliam navem conscendere, sed a parentibus est retentus. Reperta autem tertia nave,
retenere penitus non potuit. Qua ascensa, cum inpellente vento altum mare ingressi fuissent, os eius virtus sancti antistitis reseravit. Qui, extensis ad caelum
manibus, locutus est, dicens: 'Gratias tibi ago, omnipotens Deus, qui me hoc iter sulcare iussisti. Iam enim, priusquam templum sancti tui videam, eius
beneficiis sum refertus'. Quibus navigantibus, Burdigala urbe adpulsi sunt; egressusque hinc de navi, ad basilicam sancti accedens ac votum suum exsolvens, quae
scripsimus ab ipsius ore relata cognovimus.

### 41

**[041]** Alia vero festivitate adveniente, quae in hieme caelebratur, Maurellus quidam ex domo Ponticonensi, servus Agini ducis, qui mense Martio per
incursionem nescio quam unius poplitis perdiderat usum, et gressum figere non valens, adhibito sibi ad geniculum fuste, ut mos claudorum est, adfuit. Is cum per
triduum orationem fudisset ad Dominum, quarta die, quod est in crastinum de festivitate, genu directo, sanus abscessit. Poet paucos autem dies homines qui
carceris vinculis tenebantur divinitus absoluti, sancti basilicam sunt ingressi et per iudicem immunes a damno laxati sunt.

### 42

**[042]** Puer quidam, manibus pedibusque contractis, de villa Themello in pago Turonicae urbis vici Ambiacensis, adveniens ad basilicam sancti, dum inter
reliquos petentes postolaret victus stipem, visitatus a sancti virtute, directus abscessit.

### 43

**[043]** Alius quoque puerolus Euthimi presbiteri nostri, cum in valitudine febris nimiae incedisset ac exanimari ab eadem putaretur, de pulvere sancti
sepulchri presbiter levans ac fimbrias pallae superpositae disrumpens, secum detulit pulveremque puero hauriendum dedit, fimbrias vero collo illius alligavit.
Mox febre restincta, sanatus est. Non dispari modo et Ulfaricus presbiter altero puero febricitanti studium adhibens, et ille protinus febre carens, convaluit.

### 44

**[044]** Principius quidam vir bonus, Petrocoricae urbis civis, amentiam nescio quam incurrisse putabatur, et tam graviter agebat interdum, ut de sensu
videretur excedere. Quod cum multis mensibus perferret, beati antestitis basilicam expetivit; ibique, ut arbitror, quattuor resedens menses, abstenens se a cibo
carnium ac vino, adiutus confessoris beati praesidio, incolomis domui suae restitutus est.

### 45

**[045]** Et quia rusticitas hominum, dum parum praedicationem sacerdotalem sequitur, ipsa se Dei praeparat ad offensam, quae nuper gestum fuit edicam.
Leodulfus quidam Biturigae urbis homo, cum fenum secuisset, metuens, ne adventu pluviae venientis infunderetur et laborem suum perderet, die dominico, mane
iunctis bubus, ad pratum direxit ac super plaustrum fenum adglomerare coepit; statimque pes eius unus quasi ardens ei visus est, regressusque ad hospitium suum,
quievit ab opere. Post missarum vero solemnia celebrata, iterum iunctis bubus, opus coeptum pergit explere, conpletumque plaustrum fenu, statim oculi eius quasi
a quibusdam aculeis puncti, dolorem maximum intulerunt. Quibus conclusis, numquam deinceps aperire potuit. Sicque per annum integrum in caecitate permanens, ad
festivitatem sancti antistitis devotus advenit, cuius post diem tertiam beneficio lucis, quam perdiderat, restauratus est. Eo tempore et alius contractus
adveniens, virtute sancti directus, propriis gressibus ad urbem suam regressus est.

### 46

**[046]** Advenerat quidam ex Brittania nomine Paternianus, qui caecus, mutus ac surdus, manibus contractus per quoddam contagium fuerat, et confictis omnibus
membris a morbo, soli tantum pedes praebebant homini sustentaculum. Patroni praepotentis hic expetiit basilicam, orationem fudit, apertis oculis lucem perditam
cernit, manus ad usum pristinum recepit, et se salvatum beati antistitis virtute demirans, sospitatis suae gratiam populis declaravit. Ob huius miraculi gratiam
a multis munera capit, de quibus nonnullos a iugo captivitatis exemit.

### 47

**[047]** Praesenti quoque tempore apud Burdegalensim urbem domus una ignibus conprehensa vehementer coepit exuri. Cumque, flammis hinc et inde spatiantibus,
aliae domus huic discrimini subiacerent, nec esset dubium, easdem huius fomitis calore depasci, congregatus in circuitu populus nomen beati Martini coepit
attentius invocare et, ne vicinas domos virtus eius exuri permitteret, cum lacrimis deprecare; sicque ad elevatam vocem deflentium coepit crepitus flammae
decedere. Atque illis clamantibus ad caelum, advenit subito, antistite inpertiente, praesidium; conlisumque orationi supplici incendium, restinxit plebs per
lacrimas, quod nequiverat superare per undas. Eo tempore puer noster Launovaldus, cum graviter a disenteria fatigaretur, ut de pulvere sepulchri accepit,
protinus morbo caruit. [EXPLICIT LIBER IV. DE VIRTUTIBUS ET MIRACULIS BEATI MARTINI CONFESSORIS].
# THE LIFE OF THE FATHERS

## Source statement

The Latin control text is Gregory of Tours, *Liber vitae patrum*, in *Monumenta Germaniae Historica, Scriptores rerum Merovingicarum* 1,2, *Miracula et opera
minora*, edited by Bruno Krusch, second edition (1969), pp. 211–294, from the openMGH TEI transcription. The English is the project’s own translation from that
text. The printed capitula name twenty Lives; the general prologue, each Life’s prologue, every numbered subsection, and the printed explicits are retained.

## The scene

Gregory gathers twenty accounts of bishops, abbots, hermits, recluses, and one holy woman whose lives and posthumous miracles connect the ascetic households of
fifth- and sixth-century Gaul with the churches of Clermont, Tours, Lyon, Trier, Bourges, and their surrounding districts. The collection moves from founders
and teachers to enclosed solitaries, joining kinship, patronage, labour, penance, healing, visions, relics, and burial places into a single ecclesiastical
landscape.

## Kinship and same-name fences

- Life I: Romanus and Lupicinus are brothers.
- Life VI: Gallus is the son of Georgius and Leucadia; Life III identifies Gallus as Gregory’s great-uncle.
- Life VII: Gregory of Langres is not Gregory of Tours. His wife is Armentaria; Tetricus is his son and episcopal successor; the younger Armentaria is his granddaughter.
- Life VIII: Nicetius of Lyon is the son of Florentinus and Artemia and the nephew of Bishop Sacerdos. He is not Nicetius of Trier in Life XVII.
- Life IX: Patroclus is the son of Aetherius and brother of Antonius.
- Life XIII: Lupicinus the recluse is not Lupicinus, brother of Romanus, in Life I.
- Life XIV: Martius is not Martin of Tours.
- Life XIX: Monegundis’s husband and two daughters are unnamed in the text.

## Recension note

Life XIX is listed as *De Monegundis religiosa* in the printed capitula. In the MGH text its prologue follows Life XVIII without a separately printed
roman-numbered heading; the numbered title is restored here from the capitula. Life VIII.3 preserves the transmitted ellipsis after King Childebert’s answer.
Editorial square brackets belong to the MGH text.

# ENGLISH TRANSLATION

## General Prologue

**[000]** I had resolved to write only what has been divinely accomplished at the tombs of the most blessed martyrs and confessors. But because I have recently
discovered certain things about those whom the merit of blessed conduct has raised to heaven, and because I consider the course of their lives, known through
reliable reports, to build up the church, I do not delay, since opportunity urges me, to say some things about them. The Life of the saints not only discloses
their purpose but also incites the minds of hearers to advancement. Some ask whether I ought to say the *Life* of the saints or the *Lives*. Aulus Gellius and
very many other philosophers wished to say *Lives*. Pliny the author says in the third book of his *Art of Grammar*: “The ancients spoke of the *lives* of each
of us; but grammarians have thought that *life* has no plural number.” Hence it is manifest that it is better to say *the Life of the Fathers* than *the Lives*:
although there is a diversity of merits and virtues, one bodily life nevertheless nourishes all in the world. I confess that in the earlier Book of the
Confessors I wrote certain briefer things about the life of some and what they accomplished in the body. Although immense things are reckoned to belong to God’s
power, small things are rendered in writing. Unskilled and unlearned, I also presume to disclose in this book, which I have wished to call *the Life of the
Saints*, matters at greater length. I pray the Lord to deign to put a word in my mouth—he who has often opened the mouths of the mute to their former uses—and
to reckon what he commands to be written about the saints to be proclaimed in his own praises.

## I. The Holy Abbots Romanus And Lupicinus

### Prologue

**[001]** The course of the Gospel’s teaching admonishes us that the money of the Lord’s bounty, lent to the money-changers, should be restored to the Lord who
dispenses it, together with the fitting fruit of its increase. It must not be buried in deep pits and hidden away to its loss; rather, extended under a prudent
stewardship, it should grow toward the gain of eternal life. Thus the Lord, beginning his recompense and seeking with interest what he has lent, when he has
received the talents of his loan with twofold satisfaction, may say: “Well done, good servant; because you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you
over many. Enter into the joy of your lord.” For it belongs to the predestined to accomplish these things with God’s help: those who, from the very cries of the
cradle, as we often read of many, have deserved to know the Lord and, once knowing him, have never departed from his commandments, nor after the sacrament of
baptism have defiled that snow-white and glorious robe of regeneration with shameless deeds. Rightly do they follow the Lamb wherever he goes; the Lamb’s own
surpassing radiance has crowned them like beautiful lilies that wither in no heat of temptation. Over these garlands the right hand of his renowned lordship is
stretched out: it calls on those beginning, helps those striving, and adorns the victors. Marked beforehand with the title of his name, it lifts them from
earthly groanings and carries them in glory into the joys of heaven. I do not doubt that those also belong to this snow-white company of the elect who, roaming
the dark places of the Jura wilderness, deserved not only to make themselves a temple of God but also to prepare in many minds tabernacles for the grace of the
Holy Spirit: I mean Lupicinus and his brother Romanus.

### 1

**[002]** From the beginning of his life Lupicinus sought God with his whole heart. He was instructed in letters, and when he had reached the lawful age, his
father compelled him to be bound by a betrothal, although his mind gave no consent. Romanus, who was still younger, likewise desired to turn his mind to God’s
work and refused marriage. When their parents departed from the world, the brothers with one accord longed for the wilderness. Together they went into the
recesses of the Jura desert, which lies between Burgundy and Alamannia and borders the city of Avenches, and there they pitched their shelters. Prostrate on the
ground, they entreated the Lord each day with the melody of psalmody, seeking their food from the roots of herbs. But the malice of him who fell from heaven is
always accustomed to lay snares for the human race, and so he armed himself against these servants of God and strove through his ministers to call them back
from the journey they had begun. The demons did not cease to assail them with stones every day. Whenever they bent their knees to pray to the Lord, a shower of
stones immediately fell upon them, hurled by the demons, so that they were often wounded and tormented by immense agonies. Meanwhile Romanus, whose age was
still immature, began to fear the daily enemy’s injuries. Unable to endure the pain any longer, he resolved to leave the wilderness and return home. But what
does the enemy’s envy not compel? When they had left the dwelling they had sought and returned to the estates where people lived, they entered the house of a
poor man. A woman asked from what journey these soldiers of Christ had come. Not without shame, they answered that they had left the wilderness, and they
explained in order the cause that had drawn them away from the work they had begun. She said, “Men of God, you ought to have fought manfully against the devil’s
snares and not feared his hostilities. He has often been overcome by God’s friends and fallen. He is the rival of holiness, for he fears that the human race,
ennobled by faith, may ascend to the place from which he fell in base perfidy.” Their hearts were pierced, and when they had withdrawn from the woman they said,
“Woe to us! We have sinned against God by abandoning our purpose. Now a woman rebukes us for cowardice. What sort of life shall we have hereafter if we do not
return to the place from which the enemy’s cunning expelled us?”

### 2

**[003]** Then, armed with the standard of the cross and taking staffs in their hands, they returned to the wilderness. When they arrived, the devil’s malice
again began to assail them with stones. But they persevered in prayer and obtained from the Lord’s mercy the removal of the temptation, so that they remained
free and unhindered in that service of divine worship. While they devoted themselves to prayer, crowds of brothers began to gather around them from every side
and to hear the word of preaching from them. When the blessed hermits had thus become known to the people, as we have said, they made themselves a monastery
which they wished to be called Condatiscone. There they cut down the forests, reduced the land to level ground, and sought their food from the labour of their
own hands. So great a fervour for the love of God had kindled the neighbouring districts that the multitude gathered for God’s service could not all live
together. They therefore made another monastery, in which they established a swarm from that blessed hive. When these houses had subsequently been enlarged with
God’s help, they founded a third monastery within the territory of Alamannia. The two fathers went in turn to visit the sons whom they had imbued with divine
teaching, preaching in each monastery the things that pertained to the instruction of the soul. Lupicinus, however, held sole authority over them as abbot. He
was exceedingly sober and abstained from food and drink, so that he often took refreshment only every third day. When thirst seized him, as the necessity of the
human body demands, he had a vessel of water brought and kept his hands immersed in it for a long time. Wonderful to tell, his flesh absorbed the water placed
before it in such a way that you would think he was taking it through his mouth; thus the burning of his thirst was quenched. He was very severe in disciplining
the brothers and allowed no one not only to act perversely but even to speak perversely. He also greatly avoided conversation with women and meetings with them.
Romanus, by contrast, was so simple that he took none of these considerations to heart, but gave equally to men and women the blessing they asked, invoking the
name of the Divinity.

### 3

**[004]** When Abbot Lupicinus did not have enough to sustain so great a congregation, God revealed to him a place in the wilderness where treasures had been
hidden in ancient times. Going to that place alone, he carried back to the monastery as much gold and silver as he could lift, and with food purchased from it
he refreshed the crowds of brothers whom he had gathered for God’s service. He did this every year, but he disclosed to none of the brothers the place that the
Lord had deigned to reveal to him.

It happened on one occasion that he visited the brothers whom we have said were gathered in those regions of Alamannia. Arriving at midday while the brothers
were still in the field, he entered the house where food was being cooked for their meal. He saw a great array of various dishes and a large quantity of fish
collected there, and said in his heart, “It is not right that monks, whose life is solitary, should enjoy such unsuitable expense.” He immediately ordered a
large bronze cauldron to be prepared. When it had been set over the fire and began to boil, he put into it all the food they had prepared—fish, vegetables,
pulse, and whatever had been intended for the monks to eat—and said, “Let the brothers now be refreshed with this porridge; they must not indulge in delicacies
that hinder them from the divine work.” When they learned of this, they bore it with great displeasure. Twelve men, inflamed with anger after taking counsel
together, left the place and wandered through deserted regions, seeking the delights of the world. This was immediately revealed to Romanus in a vision, for
divine compassion did not wish to hide from him what had happened. When the abbot returned to the monastery, Romanus said to him, “If you were going away to
scatter the brothers like this, would that you had never gone to them!” Lupicinus answered, “Dearest brother, do not be grieved by what has happened. Know that
the Lord’s threshing-floor has been cleansed: only the wheat has been stored in the granary, while the chaff has been thrown outside.” Romanus said, “Would that
none of them had departed! But now tell me, I beg you, how many went away.” He replied, “Twelve crested and haughty men, in whom God does not dwell.” Then
Romanus said with tears, “I trust in the regard of divine compassion that he will not separate even them from his treasure, but will gather them and gain for
himself those for whom he deigned to suffer.” After praying for them, he obtained their return to the grace of Almighty God. The Lord caused their hearts to be
pierced with remorse; doing penance for their transgression, each gathered his own congregation, and they established monasteries for themselves which endure in
the praises of God to this day. Romanus continued in simplicity and good works, visiting the sick and healing them by his prayer.

### 4

**[005]** Once, while he was travelling to visit the brothers, twilight overtook him and he turned aside to a small hospice for lepers. There were nine men
there. They received him, and at once, full of God’s charity, he ordered warm water to be prepared and washed all their feet with his own hand. He also
commanded a broad bed to be made so that they could all rest in one bed, feeling no horror at the foul spots of leprosy. When this had been done and the lepers
had fallen asleep, he remained awake amid the chanting of psalms. He stretched out his hand and touched the side of one sick man, who was immediately cleansed.
Touching another again with that healing touch, he too was cleansed at once. When they perceived that they had been restored to health, each touched his
neighbour, so that, on waking, they might ask the saint for their own cleansing. But when they had been touched by one another, they too were cleansed. At
daybreak he saw them all shining with clear skin. Giving thanks to God, bidding them farewell, and bestowing a kiss on each, he departed, charging them always
to keep the things of God in their hearts and practise them in their works.

### 5

**[006]** When Lupicinus had become an old man, he went to King Chilperic, who then ruled Burgundy, for he had heard that the king was residing in the city of
Geneva. As he entered the gate, the throne of the king, who at that hour had sat down to a banquet, shook. Terrified, the king said to his attendants, “There
has been an earthquake.” Those present answered that they had felt no movement. He said, “Run to the gate as quickly as possible, in case someone who wishes to
oppose our kingdom is there intending to harm us; this seat did not shake without cause.” They ran out at once and found the old man in a garment of skins, and
told the king about him. He said, “Go and bring him into my presence, so that I may learn what rank of man he is.” Lupicinus was immediately brought in and
stood before the king, as Jacob once stood before Pharaoh. The king said to him, “Who are you, and where have you come from? What is your work, or what need
compels you to come to us? Declare it!” He answered, “I am a father of the Lord’s sheep. Although the Lord continually refreshes them with spiritual food
through his constant provision, at times they lack bodily nourishment. We therefore ask your power to grant something toward their needs for food and clothing.”
Hearing this, the king said, “Accept fields and vineyards from which you can live and supply your needs.” Lupicinus replied, “We will not accept fields and
vineyards; but if it pleases your power, assign something from their produce. It is not fitting for monks to be exalted by worldly possessions; rather, in
humility of heart they must seek God’s kingdom and his righteousness.” When the king heard these words, he issued an order that every year they should receive
three hundred measures of wheat, the same number of measures of wine, and one hundred gold pieces for purchasing clothing for the brothers. They are said to
receive this from the officers of the treasury even now.

### 6

**[007]** Afterwards, when Abbot Lupicinus and his brother Romanus were old and advanced in age, Lupicinus said to his brother, “Tell me in which monastery you
wish your tomb to be prepared, so that we may rest together.” Romanus answered, “I cannot be buried in a monastery from which the approach of women is barred.
You know what grace of healing my Lord God has given to me, unworthy and undeserving as I am, and how many have been rescued from various illnesses through the
laying on of my hand and the power of the Lord’s cross. If I depart from this light, there will be a throng at my tomb. I therefore ask to rest at a distance
from the monastery.” For this reason, when he died, he was buried on a small hill ten miles from the monastery. A great church was later built over his tomb,
and a vast multitude of people comes there every day. Many miracles are now shown there in God’s name: the blind often receive sight, the deaf hearing, and the
paralysed the power to walk. When Abbot Lupicinus died, he was buried within the monastery church. He left to the Lord the multiplied talents of the money
entrusted to him: the blessed congregations of monks devoted to his praise.

*Here ends the Life of the holy abbots Lupicinus and Romanus.*

## II. Saint Illidius The Confessor

### Prologue

**[008]** Among the other seeds of perpetual life which the heavenly Sower, from that fountain of divinity, has either poured upon the mind as an uncultivated
field by his teaching or made fruitful by his doctrine, he says: “Everyone who does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.” Likewise the
blessed apostle Paul, that vessel of election, says: “Always bearing about in your body the mortification of Christ, so that the life of Jesus also may be made
manifest in your mortal body.” Therefore Christ’s confessors, whom a time of persecution did not summon to martyrdom, themselves applied to themselves, in the
manner of a persecutor, the various crosses of abstinence, so that they might be counted worthy of God. Mortifying their members, they lived for him alone of
whom the same apostle said: “I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.” For with the eyes of the inner mind they beheld the Lord of heaven descend to the earth,
not cast down into humility but mercifully humbled for the redemption of the world. They beheld hanging upon the gibbet not the glory of the Deity but the
spotless sacrifice of the body he had assumed, of which John had shortly before foretold: “Behold the Lamb of God! Behold him who takes away the sins of this
world!” They bore within themselves also the fastening of the nails: fixed by fear of him and terrified by the divine judgments, they harboured nothing unworthy
of his omnipotence in the dwelling of their heart. That glorious light of the resurrection also shone in them: the light in which the angel gleamed when he
rolled back the stone of the tomb; in which Jesus shone within that enclosure of barred doors when he unexpectedly stood in the midst of the assembly of the
apostolic senate; and in which the same Lord, after imbuing them with words of life, was carried up into the heavenly citadel. Among these, the blessed
confessor Illidius so placed all these things in the tabernacle of his heart that he too deserved to become a temple of the Holy Spirit.

As I am about to write certain things concerning his life, I ask the pardon of my readers. No study of grammatical art has instructed me, nor has the polished
reading of secular authors trained me; only the zeal of the blessed father Avitus, bishop of Clermont, has drawn me to ecclesiastical writings. If the things I
heard him preach or read again at his urging did not fall under my judgment, I could not observe them. He led me from the reeds of David’s song to those sayings
of Gospel proclamation and to the histories and letters of apostolic virtue. From him I was able to grasp only so much: to know that Jesus Christ, the Son of
God, came for the salvation of the world, and to honour his friends with fitting service—those who took up the cross of austere observance and followed the
Bridegroom. On this subject, therefore, displaying the presumption of my raw rusticity, I shall set forth in such style as I can the things I have learned about
the blessed Illidius.

### 1

**[009]** Saint Illidius was mighty in the holiness of a perfect life and, by the Lord’s bounty, had gathered within himself gifts of various graces. By God’s
inspiration and the people’s choice, he then obtained what was still wanting to the summit of his holiness: he was chosen as priest of the church of Clermont
and pastor of the Lord’s sheep. As the fame of his holiness was carried upward through successive ascents of grace, it reached not only the boundaries of the
territory of Clermont itself but also the borders of neighbouring cities. Thus this glory came to the ears of the emperor of Trier. His daughter had been seized
by an unclean spirit and was grievously tormented, and no one could be found who could rescue her; report revealed the blessed Illidius. Faster than it takes to
tell, servants sent by the emperor found the holy old man in the aforesaid city and quickly presented him to the royal power. The emperor received Illidius with
veneration and asked about the condition of his unfortunate daughter. Trusting in the Lord, he threw himself down in prayer. After passing the night in sacred
hymns and spiritual songs, he put his fingers into the girl’s mouth and drove the wicked spirit from the possessed body. Seeing this miracle, the emperor
offered the holy priest immense heaps of gold and silver. Illidius rejected and refused them, but obtained this concession: the city of Clermont, which paid its
tribute in wheat and wine, might discharge it in gold, since those dues were brought to the imperial treasury with heavy labour. When the span of his present
life had been completed, the saint, as they say, departed to Christ in the very course of that journey. His own people carried him back, and he was buried in
his city.

### 2

**[010]** Perhaps someone, as people are often accustomed to murmur, may chatter and say, “He cannot be numbered among the saints for the performance of only
one miracle.” For if we weigh what the Lord says in the Gospel—“Many will say to me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not cast out demons in your name and
perform many mighty works?’ And I will answer them, saying that I do not know you”—he will surely understand that a miracle proceeding from a tomb contributes
more to a saint’s praise than one performed while he was living in the world. The latter may be tainted by the continual hindrances of worldly occupation,
whereas the former are entirely free from every stain. Because the deeds which we believe Saint Illidius performed before this time have been consigned to
oblivion and have not come to our knowledge, we declare what we have examined with our own eyes and experienced, or what we have learned after it was attested
by faithful people.

At the time when Bishop Gallus governed the church of Clermont, I who write these things was living in adolescence and was gravely ill. Gallus often visited me
with singular affection because he was my paternal uncle. My illness consisted of an excessive humour of the stomach together with a violent fever. Meanwhile a
desire came upon the little boy—I believe by God’s inspiration—to be carried to the basilica of the blessed Illidius. Borne to his tomb in the hands of
servants, I prayed with tears and felt lighter than when I had come. After I returned home, the fever seized me again. One day, when I began to suffer more
severely and a harsher fever than usual oppressed me, so that it lay under doubtful lot whether I would escape, my mother came to me and said, “Sweet son, I am
going to spend a sorrowful day, now that such a fever holds you.” I said, “I beg you, do not be saddened at all, but send me back to the tomb of the blessed
Bishop Illidius. I believe, and this is my faith, that his power will give joy to you and safety to me.” Then I was carried to the saint’s tomb and poured out
prayer to the Lord. Lying prostrate, I freely promised that if, through his bishop’s intercession, God would free me from this affliction, I would become a
cleric, and would not delay at all if my petition obtained its effect. As soon as I had spoken, I felt the fever depart. Calling a servant, I asked to be
carried home. When I had been brought to the couch where they were then dining, a quantity of blood burst from my nostrils, and fever and blood flowed away
together. This is proven to have been granted through the merits of the blessed confessor. More recently also, when vigils had been celebrated, a servant of
Count Venerandus, who had long remained blind, departed healed.

### 3

**[011]** Concerning his relics, I who have already been mentioned as the writer saw the following with my own eyes, just as it happened. In the first year of
his priesthood he had dedicated an oratory within the ecclesiastical residence in the city of Tours, and in it he placed relics of this bishop along with
pledges of the other saints. Many days after the dedication, the abbot advised him to inspect the relics he had placed in that altar, lest, dampened by the
moisture of the new building, some decay should have set into them. When on examination he found them affected, he removed them from the altar and began to dry
them before a fire. After arranging the bundles one by one, he came to the relics of the blessed Bishop Illidius. While he was holding them before the fire, the
thread with which they were tied, being very long, fell upon the glowing coals and became incandescent from the fire’s heat like bronze or iron. Caring little
what became of the thread, provided only that the holy relics were dried, and supposing that it had already crumbled into ash, he then saw that the thread was
unharmed. Astonished at this sight, he greatly marvelled at the blessed bishop’s power. Not without great fear, he returned the object from which he had taken
these things and revealed the glory of it to everyone. The thread was made of wool.

### 4

**[012]** There was a little boy of about ten months who, as the truth of the matter established, was regarded as a great-great-grandson of the blessed man. He
was afflicted by a very severe attack of illness. His mother wept not only for the little one’s death but also because he had not yet been anointed with the
sacraments of baptism. Taking counsel, she went to the blessed confessor’s tomb and laid the sick child on the pavement; he showed no sign of life except the
movement of his breath. She kept watch before the bishop’s tomb in vigils and entreaties. When that bird which heralds the light had sounded its clapping more
loudly with beating wings, the boy who had been cast down almost lifeless recovered. Revealing the joy of his heart with a smile, he opened his mouth by divine
power and called his mother, saying, “Come here.” Trembling and rejoicing, she approached. She had never before heard her son’s voice, and asked in amazement,
“What do you want, sweetest son?” He said, “Run as quickly as you can and bring me cups of water.” Remaining motionless in prayer until daylight came, she gave
thanks to the holy bishop, dedicated her offspring to him, and went home. When water was offered, the infant drank; released from every bond of infirmity, he
recovered completely. He then returned to the customary cries of infancy and could not speak again until, as he grew, he reached that stage of life at which an
infant’s tongue is usually loosened for speech.

I think I should not pass over in silence what happened on another occasion, when a kiln was fired to burn lime for that basilica. While those present,
including the abbot of the place, were asleep, the yoke which most firmly supported the mouth of the furnace broke. After this happened, a priest suddenly saw
in a vision what appeared to be a bishop, who said, “Hasten quickly and wake the sleepers, so that the collapse of the coming ruin does not overtake them. The
yoke that sustains the whole mass of stones is already about to fall together with the fire.” He awoke and removed everyone from the mouth of the furnace. The
heap of stones then collapsed on both sides without injuring any of those who had been standing there. I believe this was granted through the bishop’s
intercession. The priest I have mentioned prayed at the saint’s tomb; the supports were repaired, the stones were replaced, and with the bishop’s help he
completed in the kiln the work he had begun.
