## 107

**[107]** ..........

## 108

**[108]** Fuit vir vitae Paulinus Nolanae urbis [episcopus] ex nobili stirpe ortus. Tharasiam, [cum ad plenissimam venisset aetatem], similem sibi sortitus est
coniugem, habens divitias multas, et tam in fundorum possessione quam in praesidio domorum valde dives erat ac locuples. Sed cum primum aures eius euangeliorum
lectio illa penetravit, in quo Dominus adolescentem pro divitias arguit, dicens: Vade, vinde omnia quae habes et da pauperibus, et habebis thesaurum in caelo;
et veni, sequere me. Facilius est, camillum per foramen acus transire, quam divitem introire in regnum Dei, statim vinditis omnibus quae habebat, pauperibus
erogavit. Exoneratus a cunctis cupiditatibus, Magistrum liber sequitur, per haec se putans paradisi divitiae locupletari, si videretur nihil de transitoriis
possedere. Cui maiestas divina tribuit, ut quod inpossibile dixerat per euangelium, hic possibiliter adimplere mereretur per acto. Quadam vero die venit ad eum
qui stipem peteret, et ait coniugi: 'Vade et da ei quod habet necessarios'. Quae respondit: 'Non est nobis amplius quam unus panis'. Cui ille: 'Vade', inquid,
'porrege eum; Dominus enim dabit nobis victum'. Sed illa quasi strinua reservari cupiens, ne aliquid deesset, porregere noluit. Interea advenerunt quidam
dicentes, missos se a dominis suis, ut illi annonae ac vini deferrent speciem; sed pro hoc se moratos, quod orta tempestas unam eis cum tritico abstulerit
navem. Tunc vir Dei conversus ad mulierem, ait: 'Intellegi, te nunc pauperi unum panem fuisse furatam, et ideo hanc navem esse mersam'. Perrexit ergo cum
coniuge quasi peregrinaturus in alia regione, nihil habens praeter statum proprium. Post multum vero tempus, cum ab incolis regionis suae requireretur, nec
possit penitus repperiri, negotiator de civitate illa ad hanc urbem advenit, qua vir beatus caelesti Domino serviebat. Cumque vidisset eum, statim proieciens se
solo et pedes sancti amplexans, ait: 'Hic est beatus Paulinus toto vulgatus orbe, qui multum a suis civibus quaesitus, prorsus non potuit inveniri'. Et narrans
omnes actiones eius, obstipuerunt haec audientes. Nec mora, decedente sacerdote apud Nolanam urbem, ipse in loco episcopi subrogatur. Habebat autem eclesia illa
multae divitias, implevitque in eum Dominus, quae per euangelium promittere est dignatus, quia: Qui reliquerit omnia propter me, centuplum in hoc saeculo
accipiet; in futuro autem vitam aeternam poetedebit. Verum, adsumpto episcopatum, semper se humilem proferebat, quia sciebat, se apud Deum excelsum futurum, si
humilitatem sectatus fuisset. Pecunia vero de reditibus eclesiae, quae manus eius adtingebat, confestim pauperibus erogabatur. Castissima enim coniux eius non
discedebat ab eo. Erat autem vir sanctus mirae prudentiae et rethoricis litteris eruditus. Quod opus eius, de quanto ad nos pervenit, valde patefacit. Nam cum
ad diversos tam versu quam prosa scripserit, de virtutibus beati Martini sex versu conscripsit libros; scripsit et alios versiculos in lande eius. Viditque eum
in corpore positum et oculum suum ab eo inluminatum recepit. Qui tantum in virtute, multiplicata gratiarum spiritalium charismata, resplenduit, ut in obitum
suum ipsum Martinum Genuariumque Italicum, priusquam spiritum redderet, corporeis oculis contemplaret; prius enim ab eo de hoc mundo migraverant. Et quia de
huius beati vita nihil legeramus, idcirco ea quae per relationem fidelium cognovimus, dum de elymosinis proloqui voluimus, memoramus; de transitu autem eius est
apud nos magna lectio, ideo eum ex ordine prosecuti non sumus. Ecce quid tribuit elymosina! Ecce quales thesauros sanctis suis, qui se in pauperibus dilegunt,
Deus indulget! [Sicut] e contrario avaritiae malo inhiantibus quae nequiter concupiscunt aufert iuxta illud euangelii sancti oraculum, quia: Qui habet, dabitur
ei, et abundabit; qui autem non habet, quod videtur habere auferetur ab eo.

## 109

**[109]** Sic et quodam loco in portu maris gestum fuisse, multorum confirmat relatio. Quidam pauper et senex, marsupiis oneratus, venit ad litus maris; et
accedens ad portum, petere elymosinam a naucleriis coepit atque ille qui prior carinae erat inportunior adsistebat, dicens: 'Da mihi aliquid'. Tunc ille
commotus ait: 'Absiste, quaeso, decrepite, et noli nobis quaerere quicquam, [quia]: nihil enim hic aliud praeter lapides habemus'. At ille ait: 'Si lapides
dicis esse, quae in tuis ditionibus navis haec contenet, omnia vertantur in lapides'. Et statim cunctam navis onus, quod mandi potuit, in saxo conversum est.
Ego enim ex his et dactilos vidi et olivas aspexi marmore duriores. Nam cum in lapidis duritia conversa fuissent, numquam tamen colorem quem habuerant
perdiderunt, nisi eadem formae eademque species erat. Dominus autem navis paenitentia motus, inquesitum senem nusquam potuit repperire; et, sicut ferunt, per
multas civitates de his quae in saxo mutata fuerant ad videndum direxit, ut scilicet exemplum esset omnibus, ne similia perpetrarent. Ecce quid agis inpudens
avaritia! Fecisti hominem pauperem, qui non porrigendo pauperi putavit se posse fieri ditiorem.

## 110

**[110]** Quid etiam et alii contigerit, qui per adulteria multiplicare terrena studuit lucra, non sileam. Quidam apud Lugdunensim urbem vix laborans, ut unum
triantem possit habere, accensus auri exsecrabilis sacra famis, voloit per eum sacculi ora replere iuxta illum Prudenti nostri versiculum: Auri namque famis
parto conqueritur auro. Igitur de hoc triante vinum conparat, admixtisque aquis, iterum per argenteos venundatum, duplat pecuniam. Hoc iterum atque iterum agit
et tam diu turpis lucri secutor est factus, usquequo centum solides de hoc triante lucraret. Sed iudicium Dei confutavit lucra diaboli. Congerens vero avarus
negotiator aurum in sacculo, possessurus pecuniam unius horae momento, alterius negotiatoris nundinas adit Extractumque triantem, quasi aliquid negotiaturus,
conloqui cum socio coepit. Erat enim sacculum ex pelle Phoenicia, sicut his manu gestare mos est. Et ecce subito adveniens milvus, rapit eum pedibus atque
decerpere temptat, putans a colore partem aliquam carnis esse. Sed cum nihil pinguedinis sentiret in eum, evolans super alveum Araris, de quo hic aquas hauriens
vino miscuerat, laxatum sacculum deiecit in flumine. At ille, adprehensis capillis, elidens se ad terram spargensque pulverem super caput suum, aiebat: 'Vae
mihi, qui iudicio Dei oppraessus, perdidi pecuniam, quae inique fuerat adgregata! nam ex uno triante centum erexi solides. Nunc, perditis centum solidis, unus
mihi tantum remansit trians. Vae mihi, sicut feci, sic recepi; et qui de nihilo eos habui, ad nihilum redisse conspicio!' Talis pecunia, diabolae, tua est, per
tale lucrum deducis tibi oboedientibus in tartarum. Tale enim commertium et in praesenti damni notam ingerit et in futuro diversarum poenarum genera parit.
Absistite ab his, quaeso, qui haec legitis, absistite et nolite talibus participes esse! Sint lucra vestra divinae maiestatis gratia; sint exercitia vestra
Scripturae Sanctae doctrina! Fiat congregatio vestra in marsupiis pauperum, quae aeternae gehennae flagrantem restinguat incendium! et hoc ipsum a Domini est
misericordia poscendum, non propria virtute quaerendum, qui nobis praestare dignetur illorum intercessione sancta, quorum hic liber sacra prodit miracula, ut
non solum de terrenis divitiis, sed etiam de talentis verbi sui bonam facientes rationem, multiplicationis mercede recepta, audire mereamur ab ipso: Euge, serve
bone, quia super pauca fuisti fidelis, super multa te constituam; intra in gaudium Domini tui.
# THE MIRACLES OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE ANDREW

## SOURCE AND CONTROL

English translation prepared for this project from the Latin control text in Bruno Krusch’s MGH *Scriptores rerum Merovingicarum*, Volume 1, Part 2, *Miracula
et opera minora* (second edition, 1969). The MGH capitula, Gregory’s preface, and all 38 transmitted narrative chapters are included in printed order.

## SCENE AND CONTEXT

Gregory expressly presents this small book as a selection and condensation of an older, verbose book of Andrew’s miracles, which some called apocryphal. The
narrative travels from Achaia and Myrmidona through Macedonia, Thrace, Nicomedia, Byzantium, Nicaea, Thessalonica, Philippi, Corinth, Megara, and Patras. Andrew
preaches, baptizes, heals, raises the dead, confronts demons and civic violence, rejects gifts, and finally suffers at Patras. Gregory’s personal petition on
Andrew’s feast closes the transmitted narrative.

## KINSHIP AND SAME-NAME FENCE

Sostratus the Christian son accused by his mother in chapter 4 is distinct from Sostratus the Macedonian father of Philopater in chapters 24 and 26. Nicolaus
the wealthy citizen offering gifts in chapter 16 is distinct from Nicolaus the aged penitent in chapter 28. Virinus, Lysbius, and Aegeas are successive or
separate proconsular figures in the narrative, not interchangeable names. Maximilla is the wife of Aegeas; Callisto is the wife of Lysbius. The apostle Matthew
in chapter 1 remains distinct from the work’s apostolic subject, Andrew.

## RECENSION AND TEXT NOTE

The MGH capitula list forty items, but the transmitted narrative contains the preface and chapters 1–38 only. Capitulum 39, “Concerning his relics,” and
capitulum 40, “Concerning a person healed of the stone,” have no corresponding narrative chapters in this control text. They are retained in the capitula and
are not supplied with invented continuations. Gregory’s statement that he omitted tedious material belongs to the source’s own account of its making.

# ENGLISH TRANSLATION

## CAPITULA

1. Concerning the apostle Matthew and what was done in Myrmidona.
2. Concerning a blind man given sight.
3. Concerning a boy raised.
4. Concerning the boy Sostratus, whose mother brought an accusation against him.
5. Concerning Gratinus, his son, and his wife.
6. Concerning seven demons expelled from Nicaea.
7. Concerning a dead man raised.
8. Concerning a disturbance of the sea calmed.
9. Concerning robbers struck dumb.
10. Concerning those on a ship who believed.
11. Concerning the marriage of the young people.
12. Concerning Exuos and his parents.
13. Concerning Carpianus’s disabled son.
14. Concerning a dead man raised.
15. Concerning Medias’s son, his servants, and other sick people healed.

19. Concerning a serpent killed and a dead boy raised.

24. Concerning forty dead people raised.
25. Concerning a woman’s difficult childbirth.
26. Concerning Sostratus and his servant.
27. Concerning demoniacs healed at a bath.
28. Concerning the old man Nicolaus.
29. Concerning Antiphanes, his wife, and his servants.
30. Concerning Maximilla, wife of Proconsul Aegeas.
31. Concerning a disabled man healed.
32. Concerning three blind people given sight.
33. Concerning a withered man restored to health.
34. Concerning the servant of Stratocles, the proconsul’s brother.
35. Concerning the proconsul’s return from a journey.

## PREFACE

**[000]** I believe that no faithful person is unaware of the renowned triumphs of the holy apostles, because the Gospel teachings explain some of them, the
apostolic Acts narrate others, and books exist about certain apostles in which their own deeds are recorded. Concerning most of them I receive nothing beyond
writings of their passions. I found a book about the miracles of Saint Andrew the apostle which some called apocryphal because of its excessive verbosity. It
pleased me to extract and select only the miracles, omitting what generated weariness, and enclose the admirable wonders in one small volume. This would offer
grace to readers and remove the envy of detractors, because inviolate faith does not require a multitude of words, but integrity of reason and purity of mind.

## 1

**[001]** After that noble and glorious triumph of the Lord’s ascension, when the blessed apostles had dispersed through different regions to preach the word of
God, the apostle Andrew began proclaiming the Lord Jesus Christ in the province of Achaia, while the apostle and evangelist Matthew proclaimed the word of
salvation to the city of Myrmidona. But the inhabitants harshly and indignantly rejected what they heard about my Redeemer’s powers. Unwilling to destroy their
temples, they seized the blessed apostle, tore out his eyes, surrounded him with chains, and thrust him into prison, intending to kill him after a few days. An
angel of the Lord came to the apostle Andrew and said, “Arise and go to the city of Myrmidona, and rescue your brother Matthew from the squalor of the prison
where he is held.” Andrew answered, “Lord, behold, I do not know the way; where shall I go?” The angel said, “Go to the seashore, where you will find a ship;
board it immediately, for I will guide your journey.” Andrew did according to the Lord’s word, found a ship on the shore, boarded it, and sailed prosperously to
the city with favorable winds. Entering the city gate, he came to the prison. Seeing the apostle Matthew sitting in the prison’s squalor with other prisoners,
he wept most bitterly. After they prayed together, Andrew said, “Lord Jesus Christ, whom I faithfully preach and for whose name I endure so much, you who in
immense mercy have deigned to grant sight to the blind, hearing to the deaf, walking to paralytics, cleansing to lepers, and life to the dead, open your
servant’s eyes, I beg you, so that he may go to proclaim your word.” Immediately the place shook, a great light shone in the prison, the blessed apostle’s eyes
were restored, everyone’s chains were broken, and the beam confining their feet was split. All magnified God, saying, “Great is God, whom his servants preach.”
Then blessed Andrew led them out of prison and each went home; Matthew withdrew from that place. The apostle Andrew then preached the word of the Lord Jesus to
the inhabitants. Learning what had happened to the prisoners, those men seized Andrew, bound his feet, and dragged him through the city streets. The hairs of
his head were being torn out and blood flowed from his head. He prayed to the Lord, “Open the eyes of their heart, I beg you, Lord, so that they may know you as
the true God and cease from this iniquity; and do not hold this sin against them, because they do not know what they do.” Immediately great fear came upon the
inhabitants of that city. Releasing the apostle, they said, “I have sinned against you, not knowing what I was doing. I beg you, lord, forgive my offense and
show me the way of salvation, lest God’s wrath descend upon this city.” They lay prostrate on the ground before Andrew’s feet. Raising them, he preached the
Lord Jesus Christ, the miracles he had performed in this world, and how he had redeemed this perishing world with his own blood. Believing, they were baptized
in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and received remission of sins.

## 2

**[002]** Departing from that place, Andrew came into his own region. As he was walking with his disciples, a blind man approached and said, “Andrew, apostle of
Christ, I know you can restore my sight, but I do not wish to receive it unless I first ask you to order those with you to give me money from which I may have
sufficient clothing and food.” Blessed Andrew answered, “Truly I recognize that this is not the man’s voice but the devil’s, who does not allow this man to
receive sight.” Turning, he touched the man’s eyes, which immediately received light, and the man glorified God. Because his garment was vile and rough, the
apostle said, “Take off his filthy clothes and give him a new garment.” Nearly everyone began taking off his own clothing, and the apostle said, “Let him take
what is sufficient.” Thus he received clothing, gave thanks, and returned home.

## 3

**[003]** Demetrius, the leading man of the city of Amasea, had an Egyptian boy whom he loved with singular affection. A fever attacked the boy and he died.
Hearing of the signs the blessed apostle performed, Demetrius came and fell weeping at his feet, saying, “I trust that nothing is difficult for you, minister of
God. My boy, whom I loved uniquely, is dead. I beg you to come to my house and restore him to me.” Hearing this, the blessed apostle compassionately shared his
tears and came to the house where the boy lay. After preaching at length about what pertained to the people’s salvation, he turned to the bier and said, “Boy, I
say to you in the name of Jesus Christ, Son of God, arise and stand healed.” The Egyptian boy immediately arose, and Andrew restored him to his master. Then all
who had been unbelieving believed in God and were baptized by the holy apostle.

## 4

**[004]** A Christian boy named Sostratus came secretly to blessed Andrew and said, “My mother has desired my bodily beauty and continually pursues me to have
intercourse with her. I detest this unspeakable act and refuse. Moved by venom, she has gone to the proconsul to cast her own crime upon me. I know that when
accused I will say nothing in answer, for I consider it better to lose my life than reveal my mother’s crime. I confess this to you so that you may deign to
entreat the Lord for me, lest innocent I lose this present life.” As he spoke, the proconsul’s officers came to summon him. The blessed apostle prayed, arose,
and went with the boy. His mother accused him insistently, saying, “Lord proconsul, forgetting affection for maternal devotion, he turned lustfully toward me,
and I could scarcely escape being violated by him.” The proconsul said, “Boy, say whether what your mother alleges is true.” He remained silent. The proconsul
asked again and again, but he answered nothing. While he persisted in silence, the proconsul took counsel with his men about what to do, and the boy’s mother
began to weep. Blessed Andrew said to her, “O unhappy woman, you emit bitter tears over the unchastity you wished to commit against your son, whom concupiscence
has so cast down that, inflamed by lust, you do not fear to lose your only son.” When he said this, the woman answered, “Listen, proconsul: ever since my son
wished to do these things, he has attached himself to this man and has not left him.” Enraged, the proconsul ordered the boy enclosed in the sack for parricides
and thrown into the river, and Andrew thrust back into prison until he could devise tortures and destroy him too. While the blessed apostle prayed, a great
earthquake occurred with heavy thunder. The proconsul fell from his seat, everyone fell to the ground, and the boy’s mother was struck, withered, and died. The
proconsul prostrated himself at the holy apostle’s feet and said, “Have mercy on me as I perish, servant of God, lest the earth swallow me.” At the blessed
apostle’s prayer the earthquake ceased and the lightning and thunder quieted. Going around to those who lay stricken, Andrew restored them all to health. The
proconsul received the word of God, believed in the Lord with his whole household, and they were baptized by God’s apostle.

## 5

**[005]** The son of Gratinus of Sinope, while washing in a women’s bath, was severely tormented by a demon and deprived of his senses. Gratinus sent a letter
to the proconsul asking him to entreat Andrew to come to him. Gratinus himself had also been seized by fever and was gravely ill, while his wife had swollen
with dropsy. At the proconsul’s entreaty Andrew mounted a vehicle and came to the city. When he entered Gratinus’s house, the evil spirit threw the boy into
convulsions; he came and fell before the apostle’s feet. Andrew rebuked the spirit: “Depart from God’s servant, enemy of the human race.” Crying out loudly, it
immediately left him. Coming to the husband’s bed, Andrew said, “You deserve your grievous sickness, for you abandoned your own marriage bed and joined yourself
to a prostitute. Rise in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, stand healed, and sin no more, lest you incur a greater illness.” He was healed. Andrew also told
the wife, “Woman, the concupiscence of your eyes deceived you, so that you abandoned your husband and joined yourself to others.” Then he said, “Lord Jesus
Christ, I entreat your merciful compassion to hear your servant and grant that if this woman returns to the filth of lust she formerly practiced, she not be
healed at all. But if you, Lord, whose power foreknows even future things, know that she can abstain from this disgrace, let her be healed at your command.” As
he spoke, the fluid burst forth from her lower part, and she was healed together with her husband. The blessed apostle broke bread and gave it to her. Giving
thanks, she received it and believed in the Lord with her whole household. Neither she nor her husband thereafter perpetrated the crime they had previously
committed. Gratinus later sent great gifts to the holy apostle through his servants, and afterward came himself with his wife. Prostrating themselves, they
begged him to accept their gifts. He answered, “Most beloved, it is not for me to accept these things, but rather for you to distribute them to the needy.” He
accepted nothing from what was offered.

## 6

**[006]** Afterward Andrew set out for Nicaea, where seven demons dwelt among tombs situated beside the road. At midday they stoned passersby and had already
put many to death. When the blessed apostle arrived, the whole city came out to meet him with olive branches, proclaiming praises and saying, “My salvation is
in your hand, man of God.” They explained the whole affair, and the blessed apostle said, “If you believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, Son of almighty God, one God
with the Holy Spirit, you will be freed by his help from this infestation of demons.” They cried, “I believe whatever you preach and obey your command, provided
only that I am freed from this trial.” Giving thanks to God for their faith, he ordered the demons themselves to stand before him in the sight of all the
people. They came in the likeness of dogs. The blessed apostle turned to the people and said, “Behold the demons that opposed you. If you believe that in the
name of Jesus Christ I can command them to desist from you, confess it before me.” They cried, “I believe that Jesus Christ, whom you preach, is the Son of
God.” Then blessed Andrew commanded the demons, “Go into dry and unfruitful places, harming no human being at all and having no access wherever the Lord’s name
is invoked, until you receive the punishment of eternal fire due you.” As he spoke, the demons gave a roar and vanished from the bystanders’ eyes, and the city
was freed. The blessed apostle baptized them and appointed over them as bishop Calestus, a wise man who blamelessly guarded what he had received from the
teacher.

## 7

**[007]** Approaching the gate of Nicomedia, Andrew saw a dead man carried out on a cot. His aged father, supported by servants’ hands, could scarcely attend
the funeral. His mother, burdened by the same age, followed the corpse with disheveled hair, wailing, “Woe to me, whose life has been prolonged to this time so
that I must spend the provision for my own funeral upon my son’s burial.” As they uttered these and similar laments and followed the corpse with cries, God’s
apostle arrived. Compassionately sharing their tears, he said, “Tell me, I beg you, what happened to this boy that he departed from this light?” They answered
nothing for fear, but the apostle heard from the servants, “While this young man was alone in his bedroom, seven dogs suddenly came and rushed upon him. Most
wretchedly torn apart by them, he fell and died.” Blessed Andrew sighed, raised his eyes to heaven, and said with tears, “Lord, I know this was the treachery of
the demons I expelled from Nicaea. Now I beg you, kind Jesus, raise him, lest the enemy of the human race rejoice over his destruction.” Then he asked the
father, “What will you give me if I restore your son to you alive?” The father answered, “I have nothing more precious than him; I will give him to you if he
rises to life at your command.” The blessed apostle again stretched his hands to heaven and prayed, “Let the boy’s soul return, I beg you, Lord, so that when he
is raised all may abandon idols and turn to you. May his restoration to life be the salvation of all who perish, so that no longer subject to death but made
yours, they may merit eternal life.” When the faithful answered, “Amen,” he turned to the bier and said, “In the name of Jesus Christ, arise and stand upon your
feet.” He immediately arose, to the people’s amazement, and all present cried loudly, “Great is God Christ, whom his servant Andrew preaches.” The boy’s parents
gave their son many gifts to offer the blessed apostle, but he accepted none of them. He merely instructed the boy with saving words and ordered him to
accompany him to Macedonia.

## 8

**[008]** Departing from there, the Lord’s apostle boarded a ship and sailed through the Hellespont strait to reach Byzantium. Behold, the sea was stirred, a
powerful wind fell upon them, and the ship was sinking. While everyone awaited the danger of death, blessed Andrew prayed to the Lord and commanded the wind,
which fell silent. The sea’s waves quieted and calm was granted. Rescued from the immediate danger, all reached Byzantium.

## 9

**[009]** Proceeding from there toward Thrace, they saw in the distance a multitude carrying drawn swords and lances, as though intending to rush upon them.
Seeing this, the apostle Andrew made the sign of the cross against them and said, “I pray, Lord, that their father who instigated them to do this may fall. Let
them be confounded by divine power, lest they harm those hoping in you.” As he spoke, an angel of the Lord passed with great splendor and touched their swords,
and they fell prone upon the earth. The blessed apostle passed with his companions unharmed, and all threw down their swords and worshiped him. The angel of the
Lord departed from them in a great light of radiance.

## 10

**[010]** The holy apostle reached Perinthus, a maritime city of Thrace, and found there a ship hastening to Macedonia. An angel of the Lord again appeared and
ordered him to board the ship. Preaching God’s word aboard, he brought the sailor and all with him to believe in the Lord Jesus Christ. The holy apostle
glorified God that even at sea there was no lack of people to hear his preaching or believe in the Son of almighty God.

## 11

**[011]** There were two brothers in Philippi. One had two sons, the other two daughters, and they possessed great wealth because they were very noble. One told
the other, “Behold, I have outstanding wealth, and no citizen is worthy to be joined to my family. Come, let me make one household from all of me. Let my sons
marry your daughters, so that my wealth may more easily be united.” This pleased his brother. They made a compact and bound the agreement with an earnest
payment sent by the boys’ father. When the wedding day had been appointed, the word of the Lord came to them: “Do not join your children until my servant Andrew
comes; he will show you what you must do.” The bridal chamber was already prepared, the guests invited, and every wedding provision ready. On the third day the
blessed apostle arrived. Seeing him, they rejoiced greatly, met him with garlands, came forward to his feet, and said, “Admonished about you, I awaited you,
servant of God, so that you might come and tell me what to do. I received word that you would come, and I was told not to join my children before you arrived.”
The blessed apostle’s face shone like the sun, so that everyone marveled and honored God. The apostle said, “Dear children, do not be seduced or deceive these
young people, who can bear the fruit of righteousness. Rather repent, because you have offended the Lord by wishing to unite close blood relatives in marriage.
I neither reject nor avoid marriage, since from the beginning God commanded male and female to be joined; rather, I condemn incestuous unions.” Hearing this,
the parents were moved and said, “Lord, I beg you to entreat your God for me, because I committed this offense in ignorance.” Seeing the apostle’s face shine
like an angel of God’s, the young people said, “Blessed man, your teaching is great and immaculate. I did not know, but now I truly recognize that God speaks in
you.” The holy apostle told them, “Guard without pollution what you have heard, so that God may be with you and you may receive the reward of your work, eternal
life, which is bounded by no end.” Saying this and blessing them, the apostle fell silent.

## 12

**[012]** A very noble and wealthy young man named Exuos lived in Thessalonica. Without his parents’ knowledge he came to the apostle, fell at his feet, and
begged, “Show me the way of truth, servant of God, for I recognize that you are the true minister of him who sent you.” The holy apostle preached the Lord Jesus
Christ to him, and the youth believed. He attached himself to the holy apostle, forgetting his parents and giving no concern to his possessions. His parents
sought him and heard that he was staying with the apostle in Philippi. Coming with gifts, they begged that he be separated from Andrew, but he refused, saying,
“If only you did not possess this wealth, so that recognizing the world’s author, who is the true God, you might rescue your souls from future wrath.” The holy
apostle came down from the upper room and preached God’s word to them, but they would not listen. He returned to the boy and closed the house doors. Summoning a
troop, the parents came to burn the house where the young man was, saying, “Let the boy perish, who abandoned his parents and homeland.” Bringing bundles of
brushwood, rushes, and torches, they began setting the house on fire. As the flames rose high, the youth seized an ampulla of water and said, “Lord Jesus
Christ, in whose hand the nature of all elements subsists, who moisten dry things and dry moist things, who cool what burns and kindle what is extinguished,
extinguish these fires so that your servants may not grow lukewarm but rather be kindled to faith.” Saying this, he sprinkled water from the ampulla over the
flames, and the whole fire was immediately suppressed as though it had never been kindled. Seeing this, the boy’s parents said, “Behold, my son has now become a
magician.” Bringing ladders, they wished to climb to the upper room and kill them with swords, but the Lord blinded them so that they could not see the ladders’
ascent. While they persisted in this perversity, a citizen named Lysemachus said, “Men, why consume yourselves with useless labor? Do you not recognize that God
fights for these men? Abandon this foolishness, lest heavenly wrath consume you.” At his words all were pricked in heart and said, “True is God, whom these men
worship and whom I tried to persecute.” As they spoke and night’s darkness had fallen, a light suddenly shone and everyone’s eyes were illuminated. Climbing to
where Christ’s apostle was, they found him praying. Prostrating themselves on the pavement, they cried, “Lord, I beg you to pray for your servants, who were led
astray by error.” Such compunction touched them all that Lysemachus said, “Truly Christ, whom his servant Andrew preaches, is the Son of God.” Raised by the
apostle, they were strengthened in faith; only the boy’s parents did not believe. Cursing the youth, they returned to their homeland and surrendered all they
had to the public treasury. After fifty days they expired in a single moment of one hour. Because all the citizens loved the young man for his goodness and
gentleness, his entire patrimony was afterward granted to him by the public authority, and he possessed everything his parents had owned. Yet he did not leave
the apostle, but spent the produce of his estates upon the needs of the poor and the care of the needy.

## 13

**[013]** The young man asked the blessed apostle to accompany him to Thessalonica. When they arrived, everyone gathered around Andrew, rejoicing to see the
boy. When all had assembled in the theater, the youth preached God’s word while the apostle remained silent and they admired the youth’s wisdom. The people
cried, “Heal the son of my fellow citizen Carpianus, for he is very ill, and I will believe in Jesus whom you preach.” The blessed apostle answered, “Nothing is
impossible with God. But so that you may believe, bring him into my sight, and the Lord Jesus Christ will heal him.” The boy’s father went home and told him,
“Today you will be healed, my most beloved son Adimathe,” for this was the boy’s name. He answered his father, “Truly my dream has been fulfilled, for I saw in
a vision this man who would restore my health.” Saying this, he dressed, rose from his cot, and hurried so swiftly to the theater that his parents could not
keep up. Falling at the blessed apostle’s feet, he gave thanks for the healing received. The people were stupefied to see him walking after twenty-three years
and glorified God, saying, “There is no god like Andrew’s God.”

## 14

**[014]** A citizen whose son had an unclean spirit begged the blessed apostle, “Man of God, heal my son, I beg you, for he is severely tormented by a demon.”
Knowing that it would be expelled, the demon lured the boy into a secluded bedroom and strangled him, wrenching out his soul with a noose. Finding him dead, the
father wept greatly and told his friends, “Carry the corpse to the theater, for I trust that the stranger who preaches the true God can raise him.” When the
body was brought and placed before the apostle, the father explained how the demon had killed him and said, “Man of God, I believe that through you he can rise
even from death.” The apostle turned to the people and said, “Men of Thessalonica, what will it profit you to see these things if you do not believe?” They
answered, “Man of God, do not doubt: if he is raised, I will all believe.” When they had spoken, the apostle said, “In the name of Jesus Christ, arise, boy,”
and he immediately arose. The whole astonished people cried, “Enough! Now I all believe in God whom you preach, servant of God.” Because night had fallen, they
escorted him home with torches and lamps and brought him into their house, where for three days he instructed them in the things of God.

## 15

**[015]** A man from Philippi named Medias, whose son suffered severe disability, came and told the apostle, “Man of God, I entreat you to restore my son,
because his body is disabled.” He wept bitterly. The blessed apostle wiped his cheeks, caressed his head, and said, “Take courage, son; only believe, and your
desires will be fulfilled.” Taking his hand, Andrew went to Philippi. As he entered the city gate, an old man met him, begging for his sons, whom Medias had
thrust into prison for an unspeakable offense; their flesh was putrefying with ulcers. The holy apostle turned to Medias and said, “Listen, man: you entreat me
to heal your son while prisoners remain in your custody whose flesh has already been eaten away. If you wish your prayers to reach God, first release the
wretched men’s chains so that your son may also be released from disability, for I see that the malice you practice impedes my prayers.” Medias fell at his
feet, kissed them, and said, “Let these two and seven others of whom you have heard nothing be released, provided only that my son be healed.” He ordered them
produced before the blessed apostle. Andrew laid hands upon them, washed their wounds for three days, restored them to health, and granted them liberty. The
next day he told the boy, “Arise in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, who sent me to heal your infirmity.” Taking his hand, Andrew lifted him; he immediately
arose and walked, magnifying God. The boy, who had been disabled for twenty-two years, was named Philionedis. When the people cried, “Andrew, servant of God,
heal my sick too,” the apostle told the boy, “Go through the houses of the sick and command them in the name of Jesus Christ, in which you were healed, to
rise.” To the people’s amazement he went through the sick people’s houses and, invoking Christ’s name, restored them to health. All the people believed, offered
Andrew gifts, and asked to hear God’s word. Preaching the true God, the blessed apostle accepted none of the gifts.

## 16

**[016]** Then a citizen named Nicolaus presented a gilded carriage with four white mules and the same number and color of horses and offered them to the
blessed apostle, saying, “Servant of God, accept these, for I have found nothing among my possessions more lovely, provided only that my daughter, who is
tormented by severe suffering, may be healed.” Smiling, the blessed apostle answered, “Nicolaus, I accept your gifts, but not these visible things. If you offer
what was precious in your house for your daughter, how much more ought you offer for your soul? What I desire to receive from you is that the inner man
recognize the true God, his maker and creator of all, reject earthly things and desire eternal things, neglect perishable things and love everlasting things,
refuse what is seen and attend with spiritual contemplation to what is unseen. Then, strengthened in sense by this exercise, you may merit eternal life and
enjoy your daughter, restored to health here, also in the joys of eternity.” By these words he persuaded everyone to abandon idols and believe in the true God.
He healed Nicolaus’s daughter of her illness, and everyone magnified him as fame spread throughout Macedonia for the miracles he performed upon the sick.

## 17

**[017]** The next day, while Andrew was teaching, a young man suddenly cried loudly, “What have you to do with me, Andrew, servant of God? Have you come to
drive me from my own dwelling places?” The blessed apostle called the youth and said, “Author of crime, explain your work.” The demon answered, “I have
inhabited this boy since his adolescence, supposing I would never leave him. Three days ago I heard his father tell his friend, ‘I will go to Andrew, the man
and servant of God, and he will heal my son.’ Now fearing the torments you inflict upon me, I have come to leave him before you.” Saying this, the demon
prostrated itself on the ground before the apostle’s feet, left the boy, and the boy was healed. Rising, he glorified God. God granted the holy apostle such
grace that everyone came spontaneously to hear the word of salvation and said, “Man of God, tell me who is the true God in whose name you cure my sick.”
Philosophers also came and disputed with him, and no one could resist his teaching.

## 18

**[018]** While this was happening, an enemy of apostolic preaching arose and told Proconsul Virinus, “A wicked man has arisen in Thessalonica who preaches that
the gods’ temples should be destroyed, their ceremonies rejected, and all decrees of ancient law torn up. He preaches that only one God should be worshiped and
declares himself that God’s servant.” Hearing this, the proconsul sent soldiers with cavalry to bring Andrew before him. Coming to the gate, they learned in
which house the apostle was staying. Entering and seeing his face shining with immense splendor, they were terrified and fell at his feet. The blessed apostle
told his hearers what had been reported about him to the proconsul. The people came with swords and clubs, intending to kill the soldiers, but the holy apostle
prevented them. When the proconsul came and did not find the apostle in the city where he had commanded, he roared like a lion and sent twenty more soldiers.
They entered the house, saw the blessed apostle, and were so disturbed that they said nothing. Hearing this, the enraged proconsul sent a multitude of soldiers
to bring him by force. Seeing them, the apostle asked, “Have you come for me?” They answered, “For you, if you are the magician who preaches that the gods
should not be worshiped.” He answered, “I am not a magician, but the apostle of my God Jesus Christ, whom I preach.” While this was happening, one soldier was
seized by a demon. Drawing his sword, he cried, “What have I to do with you, Proconsul Virinus, that you sent me to a man who can not only drive me from this
vessel but also burn me with his powers? If only you would come to meet him and do no evil against him!” When he had said this, the demon left the soldier, who
fell and died. Meanwhile the proconsul arrived in great fury. Standing beside the holy apostle, he could not see him. Andrew said, “Proconsul, I am the one you
seek.” Immediately the proconsul’s eyes were opened. Seeing him, he indignantly said, “What madness is this, that you despise my command and subject my officers
to your authority? It is plainly clear that you are a magician and sorcerer. Now I will throw you to the beasts for contempt of the gods and of me, and then you
will see whether the crucified one you preach can rescue you.” The blessed apostle answered, “Proconsul, you ought to believe in the true God and in his Son
Jesus Christ whom he sent, especially when you see that one of your soldiers has died.” The holy apostle prostrated himself in prayer and poured out petitions
to the Lord for a very long time. Then he touched the soldier and said, “Arise; my God Jesus Christ, whom I preach, raises you.” The soldier immediately arose
and stood healed. While the people acclaimed, “Glory to my God!” the proconsul said, “People, do not believe; do not believe a magician.” They cried, “This is
not magic but sound and true doctrine.” The proconsul said, “I will hand this man over to the beasts and write to Caesar about you so that you quickly perish,
because you despise his laws.” Wishing to stone him, they answered, “Write to Caesar that the Macedonians have received God’s word and, despising idols, adore
the true God.” The angry proconsul withdrew to the praetorium. In the morning he released beasts into the stadium and ordered the blessed apostle dragged and
thrown into the arena. Seized, Andrew was dragged by the hair and beaten with clubs. Once thrown into the arena, a fierce and horrible boar was released against
him. It circled God’s saint three times and did him no harm. Seeing this, the people glorified God. The proconsul next ordered a bull released. Brought by
thirty soldiers and goaded by two hunters, it did not touch Andrew but tore the hunters to pieces. Bellowing, it fell and died. The people immediately
acclaimed, “Christ is the true God.” Meanwhile an angel of the Lord was seen descending from heaven and strengthening the holy apostle in the stadium. Burning
with rage, the proconsul finally ordered a most ferocious leopard released. It left the people, climbed to the proconsul’s seat, seized his son, and strangled
him. Such madness possessed the proconsul that he neither grieved nor said anything about it. The blessed apostle turned to the people and said, “Know now that
you worship the true God, by whose power the beasts have been overcome and whom Proconsul Virinus does not know. But so that you may more readily believe, I
will raise even his son in the name of Christ whom I preach, so that his most foolish father may be confounded.” Prostrating himself on the ground, Andrew
prayed at length. Taking the strangled youth’s hand, he raised him. Seeing this, the people magnified God and wished to kill Virinus, but the apostle did not
permit it. Confounded, Virinus withdrew to his praetorium.

## 19

**[019]** After these events a young man who was now with the apostle told his mother what had happened and summoned her to meet the saint. She came, fell at
his feet, and asked to hear God’s word. When her entreaty had been satisfied, she begged him to come to her field, where a serpent of marvelous size was
devastating the whole region. As the apostle approached, it came to meet him with its head raised, emitting great hisses. It was fifty cubits long, so that
everyone present was terrified and fell to the ground. God’s saint told it, “Deadly creature, lower the head you raised in the beginning for the human race’s
destruction, subject yourself to God’s servants, and die.” Immediately the serpent gave a heavy roar, encircled a large nearby oak, bound itself around it,
vomited a stream of venom with blood, and expired. The holy apostle went to the woman’s estate, where a little boy struck by the serpent lay dead. Seeing his
parents weep, Andrew told them, “My God, who wishes you to be saved, sent me here so that you may believe in him. Go now and see your son’s dead killer.” They
answered, “I do not grieve over my son’s death if I see vengeance upon the enemy.” As they departed, the apostle told the proconsul’s wife, “Go and raise the
boy.” Without hesitation she went to the body and said, “In the name of my God Jesus Christ, arise healed, boy,” and he immediately arose. His parents returned
rejoicing at seeing the serpent dead, found their son alive, prostrated themselves at the apostle’s feet, and gave thanks.

## 20

**[020]** The following night the blessed apostle saw a vision, which he related to the brothers: “Listen, most beloved, to my dream. I saw a great mountain
raised on high, bearing nothing earthly upon itself but shining with such light that it seemed to illuminate the world. Behold, my beloved brothers, the
apostles Peter and John, stood beside me. John stretched out his hand to Peter and lifted him onto the mountain’s summit. Turning to me, he asked me to ascend
after Peter, saying, ‘Andrew, you are to drink Peter’s cup.’ With hands extended he said, ‘Approach me and extend your hands so that they join mine, and let
your head be joined to my head.’ When I had done this, I found myself shorter than John. Then he asked, ‘Do you wish to know the meaning of what you see and who
is speaking to you?’ I answered, ‘I desire to know.’ He said, ‘I am the Word of the cross, on which you will soon hang for the name of him whom you preach.’ He
told me many other things which must now be kept silent; they will be revealed when I approach that sacrifice. Now let all who have received God’s word
assemble, and let me commend them to the Lord Jesus Christ, so that he may deign to keep them immaculate in his teaching. I am now to be released from the body
and go to the promise which the Ruler of heaven and earth deigned to make me, he who is the Son of almighty God, true God with the Holy Spirit, enduring through
eternal ages.” Hearing this, the brothers wept bitterly and struck their faces with their palms, groaning greatly. When all assembled, he again said, “Know,
most beloved, that I will depart from you, but I believe in Jesus, whose word I preach, that he will guard you from evil so that the enemy does not tear away
this harvest I sowed in you, namely the knowledge and teaching of my Lord Jesus Christ. Pray continually and stand strong in faith, so that the Lord, plucking
out every tare of scandal, may deign to gather you like clean wheat into the heavenly granary.” For five days he taught them and confirmed them in God’s
commandments. Then he stretched out his hands and prayed to the Lord, “Guard this flock, I beg you, Lord, which has now known your salvation. Let not the malign
one prevail against it, but may it merit to keep inviolate forever what it received at your command through my ministry.” All present answered, “Amen.” Taking
bread, giving thanks, he broke it and gave it to everyone, saying, “Receive the grace which Christ my Lord and God transmits to you through me, his servant.”
Kissing each and commending them to the Lord, he set out for Thessalonica, taught there for two days, and departed.

## 21

**[021]** Many faithful people from Macedonia set out with him in two ships. Everyone wanted to board the ship carrying the apostle, desiring to hear him speak
so that even at sea God’s word would not be lacking to them. The apostle told them, “Most beloved, I know your desire, but this ship is small. Let the servants
board the larger ship with the baggage, while you sail with me in this smaller one.” Giving them Anthimus to console them, he ordered them aboard the other
ship, which he kept close at all times so that they could see him and hear God’s word. While Andrew slept briefly, a man struck by a moderate wind fell into the
sea. Anthimus woke him and said, “Good teacher, help! One of your servants has perished.” Waking, the apostle rebuked the wind, which fell silent, and the sea
became calm. The wave served the man who had fallen and carried him to the ship. Anthimus grasped his hand and lifted him aboard. Everyone marveled at the
apostle’s power, because even the sea obeyed him. On the twelfth day they landed at Patras, a city of Achaia, left the ship, and stayed at a lodging.

## 22

**[022]** When many begged him to enter their houses, he answered, “As the Lord lives, I will go nowhere except where my God commands.” Sleeping that night, he
received no revelation. The next night, saddened by this, he heard a voice saying, “Andrew, I am always with you and will not abandon you.” Hearing this, he
glorified God for the vision. Proconsul Lysbius was admonished in a vision to receive the man of God. He sent to the man who had given them lodging and asked
him to bring the blessed apostle. Andrew came to the proconsul, entered his bedroom, and saw him lying with closed eyes as though dead. Prodding his side,
Andrew said, “Arise and tell me what happened to you.” He answered, “I am the one who cursed the way you teach. I sent soldiers with ships to the proconsul of
Macedonia so that he might send you to me in chains and I could condemn you to death. But they suffered shipwrecks and could never reach the place I commanded.
While I persisted in my intention to destroy your way, two Ethiopian men appeared and beat me with whips, saying, ‘I can no longer have any power here, because
the man you planned to persecute has come. Now, on this night when I still have power, I will avenge myself upon you.’ After severely beating me, they departed.
Now, man of God, entreat the Lord to forgive this offense and heal me of the illness holding me.” While he narrated this before all the people, the blessed
apostle continually preached God’s word and everyone believed. The proconsul was healed, believed, and was strengthened in faith.

## 23

**[023]** Trofima, who had formerly been the proconsul’s concubine and was now married to another man, left her husband and attached herself to apostolic
teaching. For this reason she often came to the proconsul’s house, where the apostle constantly taught. Her angry husband went to his former mistress and said,
“Trofima, remembering the unchastity she used to practice with my lord proconsul, is now joined to him again.” Inflamed with venom, the proconsul’s wife
answered, “That is why my husband left me and has not had intercourse with me for six months: because he loves his maidservant.” Summoning her steward, she
ordered Trofima condemned as a prostitute. Without delay Trofima was taken to a brothel and handed over to a pimp. Lysbius knew nothing of this, and when he
sought her his wife deceived him. Entering the brothel, Trofima prayed constantly. When men came to touch her, she placed the Gospel she carried against her
breast, and everyone approaching her immediately lost all strength. One most shameless young man came to abuse her. As she resisted, he tore her garments and
the Gospel fell to the ground. Weeping, Trofima stretched her hands to heaven and said, “Lord, for whose name I love chastity, do not permit me to be polluted.”
An angel of the Lord immediately appeared; the youth fell at her feet and died. Strengthened, she blessed and glorified the Lord, who had not permitted her to
be abused. She then raised the youth in the name of Jesus Christ, and the whole city ran to the spectacle. The proconsul’s wife went to the bath with her
steward. While they washed together, a most hideous demon appeared; struck by it, both fell and died. Great lamentation arose, and the apostle and proconsul
were told that his wife had died with the pimp. Hearing this, blessed Andrew told the people, “Most beloved, see how the enemy prevails: they condemned Trofima
to prostitution because of her chastity. Now God’s judgment has come: behold the mistress of the household who ordered her placed in a brothel has been struck
with her pimp in the bath, fallen, and died.” As he spoke, the wife’s nurse arrived, so old that others carried her in their hands. With torn garments and loud
cries she was set before the apostle and begged, “I know you are beloved of God and that your God grants whatever you ask. Have mercy on me now and raise her.”
Compassionately moved by the woman’s tears, the blessed apostle turned to the proconsul and asked, “Do you wish her raised?” He answered, “Far be it that she
should live, who committed such disgrace in my house.” The apostle said, “Do not act thus; I must have mercy on petitioners in order to obtain mercy from God.”
While he spoke, the proconsul went to the praetorium. The holy apostle ordered the body placed in the middle, approached, and said, “Kind Lord Jesus Christ, I
ask that this woman be raised so that all may know you alone are Lord God, merciful and just, who does not permit the innocent to perish.” Turning, he touched
the woman’s head and said, “Arise in the name of my God Jesus Christ,” and she immediately arose. With downcast face she wept, groaned, and looked at the
ground. The apostle told her, “Enter your bedroom and pray privately until the Lord strengthens you.” She answered, “First reconcile me with Trofima, upon whom
I heaped so much evil.” The holy apostle said, “Do not fear; Trofima does not remember evils or seek vengeance, but thanks God in everything that happened to
her.” Trofima was summoned, and Andrew reconciled her with Callisto, the proconsul’s wife who had been raised. Lysbius advanced so greatly in faith that one day
he came to the apostle and confessed all his sins. The holy apostle told him, “Son, I thank God that you fear the future judgment. Act manfully and be
strengthened in the Lord in whom you believe.” Holding his hand, Andrew walked with him along the shore.

## 24

**[024]** After walking, Andrew sat down and those with him sat individually upon the sand, hearing God’s word. Behold, a corpse drowned at sea was cast upon
the shore before the apostle’s feet. The holy apostle Andrew, exulting in the Lord, said, “This man must be raised so that I may know what the enemy did to
him.” After praying, he took the dead man’s hand and lifted him; he immediately revived and spoke. Because he was naked, Andrew gave him a tunic and said, “Tell
me the sequence and explain everything that happened to you.” He answered, “Whoever you are, I will hide nothing from you. I am the son of Sostratus, a
Macedonian citizen who recently arrived from Italy. When I returned home, I heard that a new doctrine had arisen which no one had previously heard, and that a
certain teacher who declared himself a disciple of the true God performed signs, wonders, and great healings. Hearing this, I hastened to see him, for I thought
that he who did such things must be God. While I sailed with my servants and friends, a storm suddenly arose, the sea was stirred, and I was overwhelmed by
waves. If only they had been cast ashore with me, so that they too might be raised by you as I was!” Saying this, he pondered in his heart and concluded that
this was the apostle he sought. Falling at Andrew’s feet, he said, “I know you are the servant of the true God. I beg for those who were with me, that through
your ministry they too may merit life and know the true God you preach.” Filled with the Holy Spirit, the holy apostle steadfastly preached God’s word to him,
and the youth marveled at his teaching. Andrew stretched out his hands and said, “Lord, I beg you, reveal also the other dead bodies, so that they too may know
you as the true and only God.” As he spoke, thirty-nine bodies immediately appeared, carried to the shore by the serving wave. The youth wept and everyone began
weeping. Prostrating themselves before the apostle’s feet, they begged that these too be raised. Philopater—for this was the youth’s name—said, “My father
willingly sent me here with provisions and great money. If he hears what happened to me, he will blaspheme your God and reject his teaching. Far be it that this
should happen.” While everyone wept, the apostle asked that the bodies be gathered, because they had been cast up scattered. When all had been assembled, he
asked, “Whom do you wish raised first?” Philopater answered, “Warus, my foster brother.” Kneeling on the ground with palms extended to heaven, Andrew prayed
long and tearfully, “Good Jesus, raise this dead man who was nursed with Philopater, so that he may know your glory and your name be magnified among the
peoples.” The boy immediately arose, and all present marveled. The apostle prayed over each of the others and said, “Lord Jesus, I beg that these too, brought
from the sea’s depths, may rise.” He then instructed the brothers that each should take a dead man and say, “Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, raises you.”
When this was done, thirty-eight were raised. Those present glorified God, saying, “Lord, there is none like you.” Lysbius offered Philopater many gifts and
said, “Do not grieve over lost possessions or depart from God’s servant.” Philopater remained constantly with the apostle, attending to everything he said.

## 25

**[025]** A woman named Calliopa, married to a murderer, conceived an illicit child. When the time for birth came, she was constricted by great pains and could
not bring forth the child. She told her sister, “Go, I beg you, and invoke my goddess Diana to have mercy on me, for she is devoted to midwifery.” When the
sister had done as commanded, the devil came to her at night and said, “Why invoke me uselessly when I can do nothing to help you? Go instead to Andrew, God’s
apostle, in Achaia, and he will have mercy on your sister.” The woman arose, came to the apostle, and related everything. Without delay he came with Proconsul
Lysbius to the sick woman’s house in Corinth. Seeing the woman tormented by severe pains, the blessed apostle said, “You deserve this suffering, for you married
wickedly and conceived deceitfully, and now endure intolerable pains. Moreover you consulted demons, which can benefit neither anyone else nor themselves.
Believe now in Jesus Christ, Son of God, and bring forth the child. Nevertheless, what you conceived unworthily will come forth dead.” The woman believed.
Everyone left the bedroom, and she brought forth the dead child; thus she was freed from her pains.

## 26

**[026]** While the blessed apostle performed many signs and wonders in Corinth, Sostratus, Philopater’s father, was admonished in a vision to visit the
apostle. He came to Achaia and, not finding him, proceeded to Corinth. While walking with Lysbius and others, Sostratus recognized Andrew as already shown to
him in a dream. Embracing his feet, he said, “Servant of God, have mercy on me as you had mercy on my son.” Philopater told the apostle, “This is my father whom
you see. Now ask him what he ought to do.” The blessed apostle said, “I know he has come to me to know the truth. I give thanks to my Lord Jesus Christ, who
deigns to reveal himself to believers.” Sostratus’s servant Leontius asked him, “Master, do you see with what light this man’s face shines?” He answered, “I
see, most beloved; therefore let me not leave him, but live with him and hear the words of eternal life.” The next day Sostratus offered the apostle many gifts.
God’s saint told him, “I must accept nothing else from you except to gain yourselves when you believe in Jesus, who sent me to preach the Gospel here. If I
desired money, I could have found Lysbius richer, who could greatly enrich me. Offer me those things by which you may advance toward salvation.”

## 27

**[027]** A few days later Andrew ordered a bath prepared. When he came to wash, he saw an old man with a demon, trembling violently. While Andrew watched him,
a young man emerged from the pool and fell at the apostle’s feet, saying, “What have I to do with you, Andrew? Have you come here to drive me from my
dwellings?” As the youth stood and the people watched, the apostle said, “Do not fear, but believe in Jesus my Savior.” When everyone cried, “I believe what you
preach,” he rebuked both demons. They left the possessed bodies, and the old man and youth, released, returned home. While washing, the blessed apostle
explained, “The enemy of the human race lays snares everywhere, in baths and rivers alike. Therefore the Lord’s name must be invoked continually, so that the
one wishing to lay snares has no power.” Seeing this, the citizens came and brought the sick, placing them before him, and they were cured. People also came
from other cities with the sick, who were healed and gladly heard God’s word.

## 28

**[028]** While this was happening, an old man named Nicolaus came to the apostle with torn garments and said, “Servant of God, behold, I am seventy-four years
old and have never departed from impurities, prostitution, and fornication. I was often led headlong to brothels and practiced illicit acts. For three days I
have heard of the miracles you perform and your preaching, full of life-giving words. I considered abandoning this conduct and coming to you so that you might
show me better things. But while I thought this, another inclination came upon me to abandon it and not do the good I intended. While my conscience struggled, I
took up the Gospel and prayed to the Lord to make me forget these things. A few days later, forgetting the Gospel I carried upon me and inflamed by perverse
thought, I went again to the brothel. Behold, a prostitute saw me and said, ‘Go out, old man, go out; you are an angel of God. Do not touch me or approach this
place, for I see a great mystery upon you.’ Astonished, I wondered what this meant and remembered that I carried the Gospel. Turning back, I have come to you,
God’s servant, so that you may have mercy on my errors. My greatest hope is that I will not perish if you pray for my lowliness.” Hearing this, blessed Andrew
spoke at length against fornication. Prostrating himself on his knees with hands extended, he prayed silently, emitting groans and tears from the sixth hour
until the ninth. Rising and washing his face, he refused food, saying, “I will not eat until I know whether God will have mercy on this man and whether he is to
be counted among the saved.” Fasting another day, he received no revelation about the man until the fifth day, when he wept violently and said, “Lord, I obtain
your mercy for the dead; why should this man, who desires to know your mighty works, not turn back so that you may heal him?” As he spoke, a voice came from
heaven: “Andrew, you obtain your request for the old man; but just as you have been wearied by fasts, let him too devote himself to fasting so that he may be
saved.” Calling Nicolaus, Andrew preached abstinence. On the sixth day he summoned his companions and asked everyone to pray for Nicolaus. Prostrating
themselves, they prayed, “Merciful and compassionate Lord, forgive this man’s offense.” Then Andrew ate and permitted the others to eat. Returning home,
Nicolaus distributed all he had to the needy and severely afflicted himself, taking nothing but water and dry bread for six months. Having completed worthy
penance, he departed from the world. The blessed apostle was not present, but a voice came to him where he was, saying, “Andrew, Nicolaus, for whom you
entreated, has become mine.” Giving thanks, Andrew told the brothers that Nicolaus had departed from the body and prayed that he rest in peace.

## 29

**[029]** While Andrew stayed in that place, Antiphanes, a citizen of Megara, came and said, “Blessed Andrew, if there is any goodness in you according to the
precept of the Savior you preach, show it now and free my house from the snare by which it is tried, for it is greatly disturbed.” The holy apostle said, “Man,
tell me what happened to you.” He answered, “Returning from a journey, I entered the gate of my courtyard and heard the doorkeeper’s voice wailing most
wretchedly. When I asked what these cries meant, those present told me that he, his wife, and his son were severely tormented by a demon. Going to the upper
part of the house, I saw other servants gnashing their teeth, rushing at me, and grinning with insane laughter. Passing them, I went to another upper room where
my wife lay after being most severely beaten by them. She was so disturbed by exhausting madness that, with her hair hanging over her eyes, she could neither
look at nor recognize me. I beg you to restore only her to me; I care nothing for the others.” Moved by mercy, the holy apostle said, “There is no respect of
persons with God, who came to save all who were perishing.” He added, “Let me go to his house.” Proceeding from Lacedaemon, he came to Megara. When they entered
the house’s gate, all the demons immediately cried with one voice, “Holy Andrew, why do you persecute me here? Why do you enter a house not granted to you?
Possess what is yours; do not attempt to penetrate what has been granted to me.” Greatly marveling, the holy apostle went up to the bedroom where the woman lay.
After praying, he took her hand and said, “The Lord Jesus Christ heals you.” The woman immediately rose from her bed and blessed God. Likewise laying his hand
upon everyone tormented by a demon, he restored them to health. Thereafter Antiphanes and his wife were his firmest helpers in preaching God’s word.

## 30

**[030]** The blessed apostle came to the city of Patras, where Aegeas, who had recently succeeded Lysbius, was proconsul. A woman named Efidama, already
converted through the teaching of Sosias, an apostolic disciple, approached him. Embracing the blessed apostle’s feet, she said, “Holy Andrew, my mistress
Maximilla, held by great fevers, asks you to come to her, for she gladly wishes to hear your teaching. Her husband the proconsul stands before her bed, weeping
and holding a sword so that when she breathes her last, he may pierce himself with its point.” With Efidama leading, Andrew came to the bedroom where the sick
woman lay. Seeing the governor standing with a drawn sword, he said, “Do yourself no harm now, but return your sword to its place. There will be a time when it
must be drawn against me.” Not understanding, the governor allowed him to approach. Coming to the sick woman’s bed, the apostle prayed and took her hand. She
was immediately drenched with sweat, the fever left her, and the apostle ordered food given to her. The proconsul offered God’s saint one hundred silver pieces,
but Andrew would not even look at them.

## 31

**[031]** Departing from there, Andrew saw a disabled man lying in dung, to whom many citizens gave alms so that he might have nourishment. The apostle told
him, “In the name of Jesus Christ, arise healed.” Rising immediately, he glorified God.

## 32

**[032]** Going to another place, Andrew saw a blind man with his wife and son and said, “Truly this is the devil’s work: behold, he has blinded them in both
mind and body.” He continued, “Behold, in the name of my God Jesus Christ I restore light to your bodily eyes; may he also deign to open the darkness of your
minds, so that, recognizing the light that illuminates everyone coming into this world, you may be saved.” Laying hands upon them, he opened their eyes. Falling
down, they kissed his feet and said, “There is no other God except the one his servant Andrew preaches.”

## 33

**[033]** Seeing these signs, a man told Andrew, “Servant of God, I beg you to deign to go to the harbor. The son of a sailor lies there on the shore. Cast out
of his house because of severe disability for fifty years, no physician’s care has been able to help him. He is full of ulcers and swarming with worms.” At
these words the blessed apostle followed and came to him. Looking at Andrew, the sick man said, “Perhaps you are a disciple of that God who alone can save.” The
holy apostle answered, “I am the one who restores you to health in my God’s name.” He added, “In the name of Jesus Christ, arise and follow me.” Leaving the
purulent rags in which his decay had flowed away, the man followed, with putrid matter and worms streaming from his body. When they reached the sea, both
entered the water. The holy apostle washed him in the name of the Trinity and restored him so completely that no trace of the illness remained in his body.
After receiving healing he was so inflamed with faith that he ran naked through the city, proclaiming, “He whom Andrew preaches is the true God.” Everyone
marveled and rejoiced at his restoration.

## 34

**[034]** While the blessed apostle did these things at Patras, Stratocles, the proconsul’s brother, arrived from Italy. Behold, one of his beloved servants,
named Algmana, was struck by a demon’s attack and lay foaming in the atrium. A great tumult arose. When this was reported to Stratocles, moved by immense grief
he said, “If only the sea had swallowed me before I saw this happen to the boy!” Seeing his grief, Maximilla and Efidama said, “Brother, do not be saddened; the
boy will soon recover. A man of God is here who shows the way of salvation and recalls many from illness to complete health. Let me send for him, and he will
immediately restore the boy healed.” Summoning the apostle, they begged him for the boy. Taking his hand, Andrew said, “Boy, arise in the name of my God Jesus
Christ, whom I preach,” and he immediately arose healed. Stratocles believed in the Lord, was strengthened in faith, and did not leave the apostle, but adhered
to him daily and heard the word of salvation.

## 35

**[035]** Every day Maximilla came to the praetorium, called for the apostle, and heard God’s word from him, because the proconsul had left Patras for
Macedonia. He was inflamed with great indignation against the apostle because his wife Maximilla, after receiving the word of salvation, would not have
intercourse with him. When the proconsul returned while everyone sat in the praetorium hearing God’s word, they were greatly disturbed, fearing he might do them
violence. The holy apostle prayed, “Lord, I beg you, do not permit the proconsul to enter this place until everyone has left.” The proconsul immediately felt
the need to empty his bowels. While he withdrew to the privy and delayed, the holy apostle laid hands upon each, signed them, and allowed them to depart.
Signing himself last, he too departed. Whenever Maximilla found an opportunity, she immediately came to the holy apostle, received God’s word, and returned
home.

## 36

**[036]** Afterward the blessed apostle was seized by Proconsul Aegeas and imprisoned. Everyone assembled to hear the word of salvation, and he did not cease
preaching God’s word night and day. After a few days he was led from prison, most severely beaten, and suspended on a cross. Hanging alive upon it for three
days, he did not cease preaching the Lord Savior until, on the third day, while the people wept, he breathed his last, as the reading of his passion most fully
declares. Maximilla received his blessed body, seasoned it with aromatics, and laid it in a tomb, continually praying to the Lord over him and asking the
blessed apostle to remember her.

## 37

**[037]** Manna like flour and oil with the sweetest fragrance flow from his tomb. By these the region’s inhabitants are shown the fertility of the present
year. If little flows out, the earth yields little fruit; if it issues copiously, great abundance of fruit is supplied. They say this oil runs to the middle of
the holy basilica, as I wrote in the first book of the Miracles. I have not pursued the sequence of his passion because I found that it had been written very
usefully and elegantly by someone else.

## 38

**[038]** These are the miracles of the blessed apostle Andrew which I, unworthy in mouth, rustic in speech, and perverse in conscience, have presumed to make
known. I entreat his mercy that, just as I came forth from my mother’s womb on his nativity, so through his intercession I may be rescued from hell; and just as
I began this life on the day of his passion, so may he deign to adopt me as his own foster son. Because the great part of my crimes calls me back from greater
merits, I rashly presume to ask only this: when, conformed to the Lord’s body after the judgment, he shines in glory, may he at least obtain for me, for my
immense crimes, pardon that cannot be denied.

# LIBER DE MIRACULIS BEATI ANDREAE APOSTOLI

## CAPITULA

1. De Mattheo apostolo et quae in Myrmidona acta sunt.
2. De caeco inluminato.
3. De puero suscitato.
4. De Sustrato puero, cui mater crimen inpigerat.
5. De Gratino ac filio et uxore eius.
6. De septem daemonibus a Nicea expulsis.
7. De mortuo suscitato.
8. De commotione maris sedata.
9. De latronibus obstupefactis.
10. De his qui in navi crediderunt.
11. De nuptiis puerorum.
12. De Exoo et parentibus eius.
13. De filio Carpiani debile.
14. De mortuo suscitato.
15. De filio Mediae et pueris eius aliisque infirmis sanatis.
16. De debile filia cuiusdam sanata.
17. De daemone expulso.
18. De Virino proconsule et filio eius ac milite suscitato.
19. De serpente interfecto et mortuo suscitato.
20. De revelatione passionis beati apostoli.
21. De eo qui in mari cecidit.
22. De Lisbio proconsule et fide eius.
23. De Trofimae et uxore proconsulis.
24. De quadraginta mortuos suscitatos.
25. De difficultate partus cuiusdam mulieris.
26. De Sustrato et servo eius.
27. De daemoniacis sanatis ad balneum.
28. De Nicolau sene.
29. De Anthiphanem et uxore ac servis eius.
30. De Maximilla, uxore proconsulis Egeae.
31. De debile sanato.
32. De tribus caecis inluminatis.
33. De arido sanitati restaurato.
34. De puero Stratoclei, fratris proconsulis.
35. De proconsule ab itinere regresso.
36. De passione sancti apostoli.
37. De virtute sepulchri eius.
38. De auctore libelli huius.
39. De reliquiis eius.
40. De calcolo sanato.

## PRAEFATIO

**[000]** Inclita sanctorum apostolorum trophea nulli credo latere fidelium, quia quaedam exinde euangelica dogmata docent, quaedam apostolici actus narrant, de
quibusdam vero extant libri, in quibus propriae actiones eorum denotantur. De plerisque enim nihil aliud nisi passionum scripta suscipimus. Nam repperi librum
de virtutibus sancti Andreae apostoli, qui propter nimiam verbositatem a nonnullis apocrifus dicebatur; de quo placuit, ut, retractis enucleatisque tantum
virtutibus, praetermissis his quae fastidium generabant, uno tantum parvo volumine admiranda miracula clauderentur, quod et legentibus praestaret gratiam et
detrahentium auferret invidiam, quia inviolatam fidem non exegit multitudo verbositatis, sed integritas rationis et puritas mentis.

## 1

**[001]** Igitur post illum dominicae ascensionis nobile gloriosumque triumphum cum beati apostoli praedicare verbum Dei per diversas regiones dispersi
fuissent, Andreas apostolus apud Achaiam provinciam adnuntiare dominum Iesum Christum exorsus est, Matheus autem apostolus, qui et euangelista, Mermidonae urbi
verbum salutis adnuntiavit. Sed incolae civitatis dure, indignae ferentes quae de Redemptoris nostri virtutibus audiebant ac sua nolentes destruere templa,
adpraehensum beatum apostolum, erutis oculis, circumdatum catenis, in carcere detruserunt, ut, interpositis paucis diebus, interficerent. Venit autem angelus
Domini ad Andream apostolum dicens: 'Surge et vade ad Mermidonam civitatem et erue fratrem tuum Matheum de squalore carceris quo tenetur'. Cui ille ait:
'Domine, ecce, viam nescio, et quo ibo?' Et ille: 'Vade', inquit, 'ad litus maris, et invenies ibi navem, in qua statim ascende. Ego enim ero dux itineris tui'.
Fecit Andreas iuxta verbum Domini et invenit in litore navem, ascendensque in eam, flantibus ventis congruis, prospere navigavit ad urbem, ingressusque portam
civitatis, venit ad carcerem. Videns autem Matheum apostolum in squalore carceris cum vinctis aliis resedentem, amarissime flevit, et facta oratione simul, ait
Andreas: 'Domine Iesu Christe, quem fideliter praedicamus et ob cuius nomine tanta perferimus, qui caecis visum, surdis auditum, paraliticis gressum, laeprosis
munditiam, mortuis vitam inmensa clementia largire dignatus es, aperi, quaeso, oculos servi tui, ut eat ad adnuntiandum verbum tuum'. Et statim locas ille
contremuit, et lux magna refulsit in carcere, et oculi beati apostoli restaurati sunt, et cunctorum catenae confractae sunt, et travis, in qua pedes eorum
coartati erant, scissa est, et omnes magnificabant Deum, dicentes, quia: 'Magnus est Deus, quem praedicant servi eius'. Tunc educti per beatum Andream de
carcere, abiit unusquisque ad propria sua, Mattheus autem recessit a loco illo. Denique Andreas apostolus praedicabat incolis verbum domini Iesu. Cognoscentes
autem homines illi de carceris vinctis quae acta fuerant, adpraehensum Andream, ligatis pedibus, trahebant per plateas civitatis. Iam enim capilli capitis eius
evellebantur, et sanguis defluebat a capite, et oravit ad Dominum, dicens: 'Aperi, quaeso, Domine, oculos cordis eorum, ut cognoscant te Deum verum et desistant
ab hac iniquitate; et ne statuas illis hoc in peccatum, quia nesciunt quid faciunt'. Et statim timor magnus factus est super habitatores civitatis illius, et
dimissum apostolum, dicebant: 'Peccavimus in te, nescientes quid faceremus. Rogamus ergo, domine, ut remittas nobis delictum et demonstres nobis viam salutis,
ne descendat ira Dei super civitatem hanc'. Haec enim dicentes, prostrati erant solo ante pedes Andreae. Quibus ille erectis praedicabat dominum Iesum Christum
et miracula quae fecit in hoc mundo, et qualiter ipsum mundum iam pereuntem proprio cruore redemit. At ille credentes baptizati sunt in nomine Patris et Filii
et Spiritus sancti, accepta peccatorum remissione.

## 2

**[002]** Andreas autem recedens ab eo loco, venit in regionem suam. Cumque deambularet cum discipulis suis, accessit ad eum caecus quidam et ait: 'Andreas
apostole Christi, scio, quia potes mihi reddere visum, sed nolo eum recipere, nisi depraecor, ut iubeas his qui tecum sunt conferre mihi pecuniam, de qua
vestitum habeam sufficientem et victum'. Cui beatus Andreas: 'Vere', inquid, 'cognosco, quia non est haec vox hominis, sed diaboli, qui non sinit homini isti
recipere visum'. Et conversus tetigit oculos eius, et confestim recepit lumen et glorificabat Deum. Cumque indumentum haberet vile et hispidum, ait apostolus:
'Auferte ab eo vestimenta sordida et date ei indumentum novum'. Expoliantibus se paene omnibus, ait apostolus: 'Quod sufficit, haec accipiat'. Et sic, accepto
vestimento, gratias agens, rediit ad domum suam.

## 3

**[003]** Demetrii autem primi civitatis Amaseorum erat puer Aegyptius, quem amore unico diligebat. Orta autem in eum febre, spiritum exalavit. Denique, audita
Demetrius signa quae faciebat beatus apostolus, venit ad eum, et procidens cum lacrimis ante pedes eius, ait: 'Nihil tibi difficile confido, minister Dei. Ecce
